[[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: *ya'tabiru* (they should reflect).]] ﴿...يَرَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنَّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ كَانَتَا رَتْقًا فَفَتَقْنَاهُمَا﴾ ("Have those who disbelieve not seen that the heavens and the earth were a joined mass, and We separated them?").

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Dahhak, 'Ata' and Qatada said: it means they were one thing, stuck together, and Allah separated them with air.

Ka'b said: Allah created the heavens and the earths, one upon another, then He created a wind that passed between them and split them apart with it.

Mujahid, Abu Salih and al-Suddi said: the heavens were a single joined layer, and He split them and made them seven heavens. Likewise the earths were a single joined layer, and He split them and made them seven earths.

'Ikrima, 'Ata' (*'Atiyya*) and Ibn Zayd said: the sky was a joined mass that did not rain, and the earth was a joined mass that did not produce plants. So He split the sky with rain and the earth with vegetation. A parallel to this is His saying ﴿وَالسَّمَاءِ ذَاتِ الرَّجْعِ * وَالْأَرْضِ ذَاتِ الصَّدْعِ﴾ ("By the sky that returns, and the earth that splits open," 86:11–12). The root *ratq* means a barrier or closure, and from it a woman whose vagina is sealed is called *ratq*. The root *fatq* means opening. The word *ratq*, though it describes the heavens and the earth, is in the singular because it is a verbal noun (*masdar*) placed in the position of a noun, like *al-zawr*, *al-sawm*, *al-fitr* and *al-'adl* and similar words.

﴿وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ الْمَاءِ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ حَيٍّ﴾ ("And We made from water every living thing"): this means that every living thing is created from water. A parallel is His saying ﴿وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَ كُلَّ دَابَّةٍ مِنْ مَاءٍ﴾ ("And Allah created every creature from water," 24:45).

﴿أَفَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ ("Will they not believe?"). ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا فِي الْأَرْضِ رَوَاسِيَ أَنْ تَمِيدَ بِهِمْ وَجَعَلْنَا فِيهَا فِجَاجًا سُبُلًا لَعَلَّهُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ﴾ ("And We placed firm mountains on the earth so it would not shake with them, and We made in it broad passages as roads, that they may be guided"). The words *fijaj* ("broad passages") means paths and routes; its singular is *fajj*. Then He explained it by saying *subulan* ("roads").

﴿وَجَعَلْنَا السَّمَاءَ سَقْفًا مَحْفُوظًا﴾ ("And We made the sky a protected ceiling"), protected from falling. Its evidence is His saying ﴿وَيُمْسِكُ السَّمَاءَ أَنْ تَقَعَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ﴾ ("And He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth except by His permission," 22:65). It is also said: protected from the devils, as evidenced by His saying ﴿وَحَفِظْنَاهَا مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ رَجِيمٍ﴾ ("And We guarded it from every accursed devil," 15:17).

﴿وَهُمْ عَنْ آيَاتِهَا مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ ("Yet they turn away from its signs"): they do not reflect on them or take lessons from them. This refers to the disbelievers.

﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ كُلٌّ فِي فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ﴾ ("It is He who created the night and the day, the sun and the moon; each in an orbit they float"): they move and travel. The *falak* is the orbit of the stars that contains them, and from the same root comes *falakat al-mighzal* (the whorl of a spindle).

Mujahid said: it is like the iron disc of a millstone. Al-Dahhak said: its *falak* is its path and the speed of its movement.

Others said: the *falak* is a moving, restrained wave in which the sun, moon and stars flow.

Some said: the *falak* is the sky in which that star is, and each star moves in the sky in which it was determined. This has the same meaning as Qatada's view.

﴿وَمَا جَعَلْنَا لِبَشَرٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ الْخُلْدَ﴾ ("And We did not grant immortality to any human before you"): meaning lasting continuance in this world. ﴿أَفَإِنْ مِتَّ فَهُمُ الْخَالِدُونَ﴾ ("So if you die, will they be immortal?"): meaning, will they be the immortal ones? This is like the words of the poet:

*"They soothed me and said, 'O Khuwaylid, do not be afraid!'
I said, and the faces denied it: 'Them? Them?'"* [[Kitab al-'Ain: 8/281.]]

That is, "Are they?" This verse was revealed when they said: "We are waiting for Muhammad's (ﷺ) fate of death."

﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ﴾ ("Every soul will taste death"), meaning every created soul. ﴿وَنَبْلُوكُمْ بِالشَّرِّ وَالْخَيْرِ فِتْنَةً﴾ ("And We test you with evil and with good as a trial"): a test, to see how you give thanks for what you love and how you endure what you hate. ﴿وَإِلَيْنَا تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ ("And to Us you will be returned").

﴿وَإِذَا رَآكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِنْ يَتَّخِذُونَكَ إِلَّا هُزُوًا﴾ ("When those who disbelieve see you, they take you only as a mockery"): mocking. ﴿أَهَذَا الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ آلِهَتَكُمْ﴾ ("Is this the one who mentions your gods?") with disparagement and reproach. 'Antara said:

*"Do not mention my horse, or what I have fed him,
or your skin will be like the skin of a mangy camel."* [[Lisan al-'Arab: 4/310.]]

That is, "Do not disparage my mount."

﴿خُلِقَ الْإِنْسَانُ مِنْ عَجَلٍ﴾ ("Man was created of haste"): meaning Adam. The common reciters read *khuliqa* with a damma on the *kha'* and a kasra on the *lam* (passive). Hamid and al-A'raj read it with a fatha on both, meaning "Allah created man of haste."

Scholars differed on this. Some said: his structure and creation are of haste, and he was made with it. A parallel is His saying ﴿وَكَانَ الْإِنْسَانُ عَجُولًا﴾ ("And man has always been hasty," 17:11).

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi said: when the spirit entered the eyes of Adam, he looked at the fruits of Paradise. When it entered his body, he craved food, and he leaped before the spirit reached his feet toward the fruits of Paradise. That is the meaning of ﴿خُلِقَ الْإِنْسَانُ مِنْ عَجَلٍ﴾.

Others said: its meaning is that man was created from a hastening in Allah's creation of him. They said: He created him at the end of the day, on Friday, before sunset, and so He hastened his creation before it set.

Mujahid said: Allah created Adam after everything else, at the end of the day on which the creatures were created. When the spirit gave life to his head but had not reached his lower body, he said: "O Lord, hurry with my creation before the sun sets."

Some said: this is an inverted (*maqlub*) construction, meaning: "haste was created from man," as the Arabs say: "I presented the she-camel to the watering trough," meaning "I presented the trough to the she-camel." Also as they say: "When the Shi'ra star rises, and the wood is level with the *hurba*," meaning the *hurba* is level with the wood. Ibn Muqbil said:

*"I drew back my hand from the garment, taking it,
alone, dragged over the hands of the ransomed ones."* [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 17/37.]]

He means: "I drew the garment back from my hand." Similar examples are many.

Abu 'Ubayd said: many people of meaning say that *'ajal* means clay in the language of Himyar, and they recited:

*"The acacia grows between the rocks, bright in the sun,
and the palm grows between the water and the clay."* [[Lisan al-'Arab: 11/428. The phrase is: "and the acacia grows in the hard rock. And the palm grows between the water and the *'ajal*."]]

That is, clay.

﴿سَأُرِيكُمْ آيَاتِي فَلَا تَسْتَعْجِلُونِ﴾ ("I will show you My signs, so do not seek to hasten"): hastening the punishment and asking for signs. ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَى هَذَا الْوَعْدُ﴾ ("And they say: When is this promise?"), meaning the punishment you promise us. It is also said: the Resurrection. Its implied sense is "the promised thing." ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ ("If you are truthful").

Allah said: ﴿لَوْ يَعْلَمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا حِينَ لَا يَكُفُّونَ عَنْ وُجُوهِهِمُ النَّارَ وَلَا عَنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ﴾ ("If only those who disbelieve knew the time when they will not be able to hold back the Fire from their faces or from their backs, nor will they be helped"). *Yakuffuna* means "they will be prevented." The verse is elliptical: it means, when they persisted in their disbelief and did not repent.

﴿بَلْ تَأْتِيهِمْ بَغْتَةً﴾ ("Rather, it will come upon them suddenly"): meaning the Hour. Suddenly, unexpectedly. ﴿فَتَبْهَتُهُمْ﴾ ("and it will bewilder them"). Ibn 'Abbas said: it will surprise them. Al-Farra' said: it will confound them. ﴿فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ رَدَّهَا وَلَا هُمْ يُنْظَرُونَ﴾ ("They will not be able to avert it, nor will they be reprieved").

﴿وَلَقَدِ اسْتُهْزِئَ بِرُسُلٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ فَحَاقَ بِالَّذِينَ سَخِرُوا مِنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ﴾ ("Messengers before you were mocked, and what they used to mock befell those who scoffed at them"). ﴿قُلْ مَنْ يَكْلَؤُكُمْ بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ﴾ ("Say: Who protects you by night and day from the Most Merciful?"): that is, who guards and shields you, when His punishment descends upon you. The meaning of the verse is: from the command of the Most Merciful and His punishment.

Then He said: ﴿بَلْ هُمْ عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّهِمْ مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ ("Rather, they turn away from the remembrance of their Lord"), meaning the Book of their Lord.

﴿أَمْ لَهُمْ آلِهَةٌ تَمْنَعُهُمْ مِنْ دُونِنَا﴾ ("Or do they have gods that protect them from beside Us?"). The *mim* here and in similar places is an extension (*sila*). ﴿لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ نَصْرَ أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ ("They cannot help themselves"), so how could they help their worshippers?

﴿وَلَا هُمْ مِنَّا يُصْحَبُونَ﴾ ("Nor will they be granted companionship from Us"). Ibn 'Abbas said: they will be protected. 'Ata' related from him: they will be given protection. The Arabs say: "I am your protector and companion against so-and-so," meaning a protector against him. Mujahid said: they will be helped and preserved. Qatada said: they will not be companioned by anything good from Allah.

﴿بَلْ مَتَّعْنَا هَؤُلَاءِ﴾ ("Rather, We provided for these disbelievers and their fathers") ﴿وَآبَاءَهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيَا حَتَّى طَالَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْعُمُرُ﴾ ("in this world until their lives were prolonged"). ﴿أَفَلَا يَرَوْنَ أَنَّا نَأْتِي الْأَرْضَ نَنْقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَا﴾ ("Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its edges?"), meaning: what We diminish from the edges of the polytheists, and increase in the edges of the believers.

﴿أَفَهُمُ الْغَالِبُونَ﴾ ("Are they the victors?") or are We? ﴿قُلْ إِنَّمَا أُنْذِرُكُمْ بِالْوَحْيِ﴾ ("Say: I only warn you by revelation"), by the Qur'an. ﴿وَلَا يَسْمَعُ الصُّمُّ الدُّعَاءَ﴾ ("And the deaf do not hear the call").

Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami read *yusma'u* with a damma on the *ya'* and a fatha on the *mim*. The damma indicates the passive, in the sense that this is not done to them, according to the convention of an unnamed agent.

Ibn 'Amir read *tusma'u* with a damma on the *ta'* and a kasra on the *mim*, with *al-summu* in the accusative, making the address to the Prophet (peace be upon him). The rest read *yasma'u* with a fatha on the *ya'* and on the *mim*, with *al-summu* in the nominative, meaning the action belongs to them. ﴿إِذَا مَا يُنْذَرُونَ﴾ ("when they are warned"), meaning frightened and cautioned.

﴿وَلَئِنْ مَسَّتْهُمْ نَفْحَةٌ مِنْ عَذَابِ رَبِّكَ﴾ ("And if even a breath of your Lord's punishment touches them"). Ibn 'Abbas said: a portion. Muqatil and Qatada said: a punishment. Ibn Kaysan said: a little. Ibn Jurayj said: a share, from the saying of the Arabs: "So-and-so *nafaha* to so-and-so" when he gave him a share [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: "from his wealth."]] and a portion of it. Some said: a blow, from the Arabs' saying: "The animal *nafahat* with its leg" when it kicked with it. The poet said:

*"And a woman of the finest women,
whose sleeves are perfumed with musk."* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/293.]]

﴿لَيَقُولُنَّ يَا وَيْلَنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَالِمِينَ﴾ ("They will surely say: Woe to us! We were indeed wrongdoers").

﴿وَنَضَعُ الْمَوَازِينَ الْقِسْطَ﴾ ("And We will set up the scales of justice"), meaning the reckoning. The word *qist* (justice) is singular though *mawazin* is plural, because it is in the sense of justice and contentment.

Mujahid said: this is an image, and by the scale He means justice.

﴿فَلَا تُظْلَمُ نَفْسٌ شَيْئًا﴾ ("So no soul will be wronged in anything"): nothing is reduced from its good deeds nor added to its bad deeds.

It is reported that Dawud (peace be upon him) asked his Lord to show him the scale, and He showed it to him. When he saw it, he fainted, then recovered and said: "My God, who can fill its pan with good deeds?" He said: "O Dawud, when I am pleased with My servant, I fill it with a date."

If it is asked: how can this verse be reconciled with His saying ﴿فَلَا نُقِيمُ لَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَزْنًا﴾ ("We will not give them any weight on the Day of Resurrection," 18:105)? The answer: its meaning is: We will not weigh them (*nuqawwimuha*), and they will not be upright in truth, [the one who questioned him is the one who deficient, as in the manuscript], because they are false.

﴿وَإِنْ كَانَ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍ مِنْ خَرْدَلٍ﴾ ("Even if it is the weight of a grain of mustard seed"). The people of Medina read *mithqalu* in the nominative, meaning "even if it falls," with no predicate. The rest read it in the accusative, meaning "even if that thing is of the weight of a grain." A similar construction is in Surah Luqman: ﴿أَتَيْنَا بِهَا﴾ ("We bring it," 31:16), meaning "We bring it into account." Mujahid read *atayna* with a long vowel, meaning "We reward it." ﴿وَكَفَى بِنَا حَاسِبِينَ﴾ ("And We are sufficient as reckoners").

﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى وَهَارُونَ الْفُرْقَانَ﴾ ("We gave Musa and Harun the Criterion"), meaning the Book that distinguishes truth from falsehood, which is the Torah.

Ibn Zayd said: it is victory over enemies. The evidence is His saying ﴿وَمَا أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَى عَبْدِنَا يَوْمَ الْفُرْقَانِ﴾ ("And what We sent down to Our servant on the Day of the Criterion," 8:41), meaning the day of Badr. This view is closer to the apparent meaning of the verse, because of the waw entering on *al-diya'* [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: so the meaning of the verse is: And We gave Musa and Harun victory and the Torah, which is the light and the reminder for the God-fearing.]] and *al-dhikr* (the reminder) for the God-fearing. On this interpretation, the waw is extra and superfluous, like His saying ﴿بِزِينَةٍ الْكَوَاكِبِ وَحِفْظًا﴾ ("With an adornment of the stars, and as a protection," 37:6–7).

It is reported that 'Ikrima used to say about this verse: its meaning is: "We gave Musa and Harun the Criterion, a light." He would say: move this waw to His saying ﴿الَّذِينَ يَحْمِلُونَ الْعَرْشَ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهُ﴾ ("Those who bear the Throne and those around it," 40:7).

﴿الَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ بِالْغَيْبِ﴾ ("Those who fear their Lord unseen"), meaning they fear Him though they have not seen Him, ﴿وَهُمْ مِنَ السَّاعَةِ مُشْفِقُونَ﴾ ("and they are apprehensive of the Hour").

﴿وَهَذَا ذِكْرٌ مُبَارَكٌ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ﴾ ("And this is a blessed reminder which We have sent down"), meaning the Qur'an. ﴿أَفَأَنْتُمْ لَهُ مُنْكِرُونَ﴾ ("Will you then deny it?"), meaning: rejecting and denying.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 21, verses 30–50:

﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَ﴾ The common reciters read it with a waw (*awa lam yara*, "Have not seen"). Ibn Kathir read *a-lam yara* (without the waw), and it is written so in their codices. [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: *ya'tabiru* (they should reflect).]] ﴿...يَرَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنَّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ كَانَتَا رَتْقًا فَفَتَقْنَاهُمَا﴾ ("Have those who disbelieve not seen that the heavens and the earth were a joined mass, and We separated them?").

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Dahhak, 'Ata' and Qatada said: it means they were one thing, stuck together, and Allah separated them with air.

Ka'b said: Allah created the heavens and the earths, one upon another, then He created a wind that passed between them and split them apart with it.

Mujahid, Abu Salih and al-Suddi said: the heavens were a single joined layer, and He split them and made them seven heavens. Likewise the earths were a single joined layer, and He split them and made them seven earths.

'Ikrima, 'Ata' (*'Atiyya*) and Ibn Zayd said: the sky was a joined mass that did not rain, and the earth was a joined mass that did not produce plants. So He split the sky with rain and the earth with vegetation. A parallel to this is His saying ﴿وَالسَّمَاءِ ذَاتِ الرَّجْعِ * وَالْأَرْضِ ذَاتِ الصَّدْعِ﴾ ("By the sky that returns, and the earth that splits open," 86:11–12). The root *ratq* means a barrier or closure, and from it a woman whose vagina is sealed is called *ratq*. The root *fatq* means opening. The word *ratq*, though it describes the heavens and the earth, is in the singular because it is a verbal noun (*masdar*) placed in the position of a noun, like *al-zawr*, *al-sawm*, *al-fitr* and *al-'adl* and similar words.

﴿وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ الْمَاءِ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ حَيٍّ﴾ ("And We made from water every living thing"): this means that every living thing is created from water. A parallel is His saying ﴿وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَ كُلَّ دَابَّةٍ مِنْ مَاءٍ﴾ ("And Allah created every creature from water," 24:45).

﴿أَفَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ ("Will they not believe?"). ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا فِي الْأَرْضِ رَوَاسِيَ أَنْ تَمِيدَ بِهِمْ وَجَعَلْنَا فِيهَا فِجَاجًا سُبُلًا لَعَلَّهُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ﴾ ("And We placed firm mountains on the earth so it would not shake with them, and We made in it broad passages as roads, that they may be guided"). The words *fijaj* ("broad passages") means paths and routes; its singular is *fajj*. Then He explained it by saying *subulan* ("roads").

﴿وَجَعَلْنَا السَّمَاءَ سَقْفًا مَحْفُوظًا﴾ ("And We made the sky a protected ceiling"), protected from falling. Its evidence is His saying ﴿وَيُمْسِكُ السَّمَاءَ أَنْ تَقَعَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ﴾ ("And He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth except by His permission," 22:65). It is also said: protected from the devils, as evidenced by His saying ﴿وَحَفِظْنَاهَا مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ رَجِيمٍ﴾ ("And We guarded it from every accursed devil," 15:17).

﴿وَهُمْ عَنْ آيَاتِهَا مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ ("Yet they turn away from its signs"): they do not reflect on them or take lessons from them. This refers to the disbelievers.

﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ كُلٌّ فِي فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ﴾ ("It is He who created the night and the day, the sun and the moon; each in an orbit they float"): they move and travel. The *falak* is the orbit of the stars that contains them, and from the same root comes *falakat al-mighzal* (the whorl of a spindle).

Mujahid said: it is like the iron disc of a millstone. Al-Dahhak said: its *falak* is its path and the speed of its movement.

Others said: the *falak* is a moving, restrained wave in which the sun, moon and stars flow.

Some said: the *falak* is the sky in which that star is, and each star moves in the sky in which it was determined. This has the same meaning as Qatada's view.

﴿وَمَا جَعَلْنَا لِبَشَرٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ الْخُلْدَ﴾ ("And We did not grant immortality to any human before you"): meaning lasting continuance in this world. ﴿أَفَإِنْ مِتَّ فَهُمُ الْخَالِدُونَ﴾ ("So if you die, will they be immortal?"): meaning, will they be the immortal ones? This is like the words of the poet:

*"They soothed me and said, 'O Khuwaylid, do not be afraid!'
I said, and the faces denied it: 'Them? Them?'"* [[Kitab al-'Ain: 8/281.]]

That is, "Are they?" This verse was revealed when they said: "We are waiting for Muhammad's (ﷺ) fate of death."

﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ﴾ ("Every soul will taste death"), meaning every created soul. ﴿وَنَبْلُوكُمْ بِالشَّرِّ وَالْخَيْرِ فِتْنَةً﴾ ("And We test you with evil and with good as a trial"): a test, to see how you give thanks for what you love and how you endure what you hate. ﴿وَإِلَيْنَا تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ ("And to Us you will be returned").

﴿وَإِذَا رَآكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِنْ يَتَّخِذُونَكَ إِلَّا هُزُوًا﴾ ("When those who disbelieve see you, they take you only as a mockery"): mocking. ﴿أَهَذَا الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ آلِهَتَكُمْ﴾ ("Is this the one who mentions your gods?") with disparagement and reproach. 'Antara said:

*"Do not mention my horse, or what I have fed him,
or your skin will be like the skin of a mangy camel."* [[Lisan al-'Arab: 4/310.]]

That is, "Do not disparage my mount."

﴿خُلِقَ الْإِنْسَانُ مِنْ عَجَلٍ﴾ ("Man was created of haste"): meaning Adam. The common reciters read *khuliqa* with a damma on the *kha'* and a kasra on the *lam* (passive). Hamid and al-A'raj read it with a fatha on both, meaning "Allah created man of haste."

Scholars differed on this. Some said: his structure and creation are of haste, and he was made with it. A parallel is His saying ﴿وَكَانَ الْإِنْسَانُ عَجُولًا﴾ ("And man has always been hasty," 17:11).

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi said: when the spirit entered the eyes of Adam, he looked at the fruits of Paradise. When it entered his body, he craved food, and he leaped before the spirit reached his feet toward the fruits of Paradise. That is the meaning of ﴿خُلِقَ الْإِنْسَانُ مِنْ عَجَلٍ﴾.

Others said: its meaning is that man was created from a hastening in Allah's creation of him. They said: He created him at the end of the day, on Friday, before sunset, and so He hastened his creation before it set.

Mujahid said: Allah created Adam after everything else, at the end of the day on which the creatures were created. When the spirit gave life to his head but had not reached his lower body, he said: "O Lord, hurry with my creation before the sun sets."

Some said: this is an inverted (*maqlub*) construction, meaning: "haste was created from man," as the Arabs say: "I presented the she-camel to the watering trough," meaning "I presented the trough to the she-camel." Also as they say: "When the Shi'ra star rises, and the wood is level with the *hurba*," meaning the *hurba* is level with the wood. Ibn Muqbil said:

*"I drew back my hand from the garment, taking it,
alone, dragged over the hands of the ransomed ones."* [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 17/37.]]

He means: "I drew the garment back from my hand." Similar examples are many.

Abu 'Ubayd said: many people of meaning say that *'ajal* means clay in the language of Himyar, and they recited:

*"The acacia grows between the rocks, bright in the sun,
and the palm grows between the water and the clay."* [[Lisan al-'Arab: 11/428. The phrase is: "and the acacia grows in the hard rock. And the palm grows between the water and the *'ajal*."]]

That is, clay.

﴿سَأُرِيكُمْ آيَاتِي فَلَا تَسْتَعْجِلُونِ﴾ ("I will show you My signs, so do not seek to hasten"): hastening the punishment and asking for signs. ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَى هَذَا الْوَعْدُ﴾ ("And they say: When is this promise?"), meaning the punishment you promise us. It is also said: the Resurrection. Its implied sense is "the promised thing." ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ ("If you are truthful").

Allah said: ﴿لَوْ يَعْلَمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا حِينَ لَا يَكُفُّونَ عَنْ وُجُوهِهِمُ النَّارَ وَلَا عَنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ﴾ ("If only those who disbelieve knew the time when they will not be able to hold back the Fire from their faces or from their backs, nor will they be helped"). *Yakuffuna* means "they will be prevented." The verse is elliptical: it means, when they persisted in their disbelief and did not repent.

﴿بَلْ تَأْتِيهِمْ بَغْتَةً﴾ ("Rather, it will come upon them suddenly"): meaning the Hour. Suddenly, unexpectedly. ﴿فَتَبْهَتُهُمْ﴾ ("and it will bewilder them"). Ibn 'Abbas said: it will surprise them. Al-Farra' said: it will confound them. ﴿فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ رَدَّهَا وَلَا هُمْ يُنْظَرُونَ﴾ ("They will not be able to avert it, nor will they be reprieved").

﴿وَلَقَدِ اسْتُهْزِئَ بِرُسُلٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ فَحَاقَ بِالَّذِينَ سَخِرُوا مِنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ﴾ ("Messengers before you were mocked, and what they used to mock befell those who scoffed at them"). ﴿قُلْ مَنْ يَكْلَؤُكُمْ بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ﴾ ("Say: Who protects you by night and day from the Most Merciful?"): that is, who guards and shields you, when His punishment descends upon you. The meaning of the verse is: from the command of the Most Merciful and His punishment.

Then He said: ﴿بَلْ هُمْ عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّهِمْ مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ ("Rather, they turn away from the remembrance of their Lord"), meaning the Book of their Lord.

﴿أَمْ لَهُمْ آلِهَةٌ تَمْنَعُهُمْ مِنْ دُونِنَا﴾ ("Or do they have gods that protect them from beside Us?"). The *mim* here and in similar places is an extension (*sila*). ﴿لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ نَصْرَ أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ ("They cannot help themselves"), so how could they help their worshippers?

﴿وَلَا هُمْ مِنَّا يُصْحَبُونَ﴾ ("Nor will they be granted companionship from Us"). Ibn 'Abbas said: they will be protected. 'Ata' related from him: they will be given protection. The Arabs say: "I am your protector and companion against so-and-so," meaning a protector against him. Mujahid said: they will be helped and preserved. Qatada said: they will not be companioned by anything good from Allah.

﴿بَلْ مَتَّعْنَا هَؤُلَاءِ﴾ ("Rather, We provided for these disbelievers and their fathers") ﴿وَآبَاءَهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيَا حَتَّى طَالَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْعُمُرُ﴾ ("in this world until their lives were prolonged"). ﴿أَفَلَا يَرَوْنَ أَنَّا نَأْتِي الْأَرْضَ نَنْقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَا﴾ ("Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its edges?"), meaning: what We diminish from the edges of the polytheists, and increase in the edges of the believers.

﴿أَفَهُمُ الْغَالِبُونَ﴾ ("Are they the victors?") or are We? ﴿قُلْ إِنَّمَا أُنْذِرُكُمْ بِالْوَحْيِ﴾ ("Say: I only warn you by revelation"), by the Qur'an. ﴿وَلَا يَسْمَعُ الصُّمُّ الدُّعَاءَ﴾ ("And the deaf do not hear the call").

Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami read *yusma'u* with a damma on the *ya'* and a fatha on the *mim*. The damma indicates the passive, in the sense that this is not done to them, according to the convention of an unnamed agent.

Ibn 'Amir read *tusma'u* with a damma on the *ta'* and a kasra on the *mim*, with *al-summu* in the accusative, making the address to the Prophet (peace be upon him). The rest read *yasma'u* with a fatha on the *ya'* and on the *mim*, with *al-summu* in the nominative, meaning the action belongs to them. ﴿إِذَا مَا يُنْذَرُونَ﴾ ("when they are warned"), meaning frightened and cautioned.

﴿وَلَئِنْ مَسَّتْهُمْ نَفْحَةٌ مِنْ عَذَابِ رَبِّكَ﴾ ("And if even a breath of your Lord's punishment touches them"). Ibn 'Abbas said: a portion. Muqatil and Qatada said: a punishment. Ibn Kaysan said: a little. Ibn Jurayj said: a share, from the saying of the Arabs: "So-and-so *nafaha* to so-and-so" when he gave him a share [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: "from his wealth."]] and a portion of it. Some said: a blow, from the Arabs' saying: "The animal *nafahat* with its leg" when it kicked with it. The poet said:

*"And a woman of the finest women,
whose sleeves are perfumed with musk."* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/293.]]

﴿لَيَقُولُنَّ يَا وَيْلَنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَالِمِينَ﴾ ("They will surely say: Woe to us! We were indeed wrongdoers").

﴿وَنَضَعُ الْمَوَازِينَ الْقِسْطَ﴾ ("And We will set up the scales of justice"), meaning the reckoning. The word *qist* (justice) is singular though *mawazin* is plural, because it is in the sense of justice and contentment.

Mujahid said: this is an image, and by the scale He means justice.

﴿فَلَا تُظْلَمُ نَفْسٌ شَيْئًا﴾ ("So no soul will be wronged in anything"): nothing is reduced from its good deeds nor added to its bad deeds.

It is reported that Dawud (peace be upon him) asked his Lord to show him the scale, and He showed it to him. When he saw it, he fainted, then recovered and said: "My God, who can fill its pan with good deeds?" He said: "O Dawud, when I am pleased with My servant, I fill it with a date."

If it is asked: how can this verse be reconciled with His saying ﴿فَلَا نُقِيمُ لَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَزْنًا﴾ ("We will not give them any weight on the Day of Resurrection," 18:105)? The answer: its meaning is: We will not weigh them (*nuqawwimuha*), and they will not be upright in truth, [the one who questioned him is the one who deficient, as in the manuscript], because they are false.

﴿وَإِنْ كَانَ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍ مِنْ خَرْدَلٍ﴾ ("Even if it is the weight of a grain of mustard seed"). The people of Medina read *mithqalu* in the nominative, meaning "even if it falls," with no predicate. The rest read it in the accusative, meaning "even if that thing is of the weight of a grain." A similar construction is in Surah Luqman: ﴿أَتَيْنَا بِهَا﴾ ("We bring it," 31:16), meaning "We bring it into account." Mujahid read *atayna* with a long vowel, meaning "We reward it." ﴿وَكَفَى بِنَا حَاسِبِينَ﴾ ("And We are sufficient as reckoners").

﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى وَهَارُونَ الْفُرْقَانَ﴾ ("We gave Musa and Harun the Criterion"), meaning the Book that distinguishes truth from falsehood, which is the Torah.

Ibn Zayd said: it is victory over enemies. The evidence is His saying ﴿وَمَا أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَى عَبْدِنَا يَوْمَ الْفُرْقَانِ﴾ ("And what We sent down to Our servant on the Day of the Criterion," 8:41), meaning the day of Badr. This view is closer to the apparent meaning of the verse, because of the waw entering on *al-diya'* [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: so the meaning of the verse is: And We gave Musa and Harun victory and the Torah, which is the light and the reminder for the God-fearing.]] and *al-dhikr* (the reminder) for the God-fearing. On this interpretation, the waw is extra and superfluous, like His saying ﴿بِزِينَةٍ الْكَوَاكِبِ وَحِفْظًا﴾ ("With an adornment of the stars, and as a protection," 37:6–7).

It is reported that 'Ikrima used to say about this verse: its meaning is: "We gave Musa and Harun the Criterion, a light." He would say: move this waw to His saying ﴿الَّذِينَ يَحْمِلُونَ الْعَرْشَ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهُ﴾ ("Those who bear the Throne and those around it," 40:7).

﴿الَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ بِالْغَيْبِ﴾ ("Those who fear their Lord unseen"), meaning they fear Him though they have not seen Him, ﴿وَهُمْ مِنَ السَّاعَةِ مُشْفِقُونَ﴾ ("and they are apprehensive of the Hour").

﴿وَهَذَا ذِكْرٌ مُبَارَكٌ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ﴾ ("And this is a blessed reminder which We have sent down"), meaning the Qur'an. ﴿أَفَأَنْتُمْ لَهُ مُنْكِرُونَ﴾ ("Will you then deny it?"), meaning: rejecting and denying.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 21, verses 30–50:

﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَ﴾ The common reciters read it with a waw (*awa lam yara*, "Have not seen"). Ibn Kathir read *a-lam yara* (without the waw), and it is written so in their codices. [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: *ya'tabiru* (they should reflect).]] ﴿...يَرَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنَّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ كَانَتَا رَتْقًا فَفَتَقْنَاهُمَا﴾ ("Have those who disbelieve not seen that the heavens and the earth were a joined mass, and We separated them?").

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Dahhak, 'Ata' and Qatada said: it means they were one thing, stuck together, and Allah separated them with air.

Ka'b said: Allah created the heavens and the earths, one upon another, then He created a wind that passed between them and split them apart with it.

Mujahid, Abu Salih and al-Suddi said: the heavens were a single joined layer, and He split them and made them seven heavens. Likewise the earths were a single joined layer, and He split them and made them seven earths.

'Ikrima, 'Ata' (*'Atiyya*) and Ibn Zayd said: the sky was a joined mass that did not rain, and the earth was a joined mass that did not produce plants. So He split the sky with rain and the earth with vegetation. A parallel to this is His saying ﴿وَالسَّمَاءِ ذَاتِ الرَّجْعِ * وَالْأَرْضِ ذَاتِ الصَّدْعِ﴾ ("By the sky that returns, and the earth that splits open," 86:11–12). The root *ratq* means a barrier or closure, and from it a woman whose vagina is sealed is called *ratq*. The root *fatq* means opening. The word *ratq*, though it describes the heavens and the earth, is in the singular because it is a verbal noun (*masdar*) placed in the position of a noun, like *al-zawr*, *al-sawm*, *al-fitr* and *al-'adl* and similar words.

﴿وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ الْمَاءِ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ حَيٍّ﴾ ("And We made from water every living thing"): this means that every living thing is created from water. A parallel is His saying ﴿وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَ كُلَّ دَابَّةٍ مِنْ مَاءٍ﴾ ("And Allah created every creature from water," 24:45).

﴿أَفَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ ("Will they not believe?"). ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا فِي الْأَرْضِ رَوَاسِيَ أَنْ تَمِيدَ بِهِمْ وَجَعَلْنَا فِيهَا فِجَاجًا سُبُلًا لَعَلَّهُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ﴾ ("And We placed firm mountains on the earth so it would not shake with them, and We made in it broad passages as roads, that they may be guided"). The words *fijaj* ("broad passages") means paths and routes; its singular is *fajj*. Then He explained it by saying *subulan* ("roads").

﴿وَجَعَلْنَا السَّمَاءَ سَقْفًا مَحْفُوظًا﴾ ("And We made the sky a protected ceiling"), protected from falling. Its evidence is His saying ﴿وَيُمْسِكُ السَّمَاءَ أَنْ تَقَعَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ﴾ ("And He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth except by His permission," 22:65). It is also said: protected from the devils, as evidenced by His saying ﴿وَحَفِظْنَاهَا مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ رَجِيمٍ﴾ ("And We guarded it from every accursed devil," 15:17).

﴿وَهُمْ عَنْ آيَاتِهَا مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ ("Yet they turn away from its signs"): they do not reflect on them or take lessons from them. This refers to the disbelievers.

﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ كُلٌّ فِي فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ﴾ ("It is He who created the night and the day, the sun and the moon; each in an orbit they float"): they move and travel. The *falak* is the orbit of the stars that contains them, and from the same root comes *falakat al-mighzal* (the whorl of a spindle).

Mujahid said: it is like the iron disc of a millstone. Al-Dahhak said: its *falak* is its path and the speed of its movement.

Others said: the *falak* is a moving, restrained wave in which the sun, moon and stars flow.

Some said: the *falak* is the sky in which that star is, and each star moves in the sky in which it was determined. This has the same meaning as Qatada's view.

﴿وَمَا جَعَلْنَا لِبَشَرٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ الْخُلْدَ﴾ ("And We did not grant immortality to any human before you"): meaning lasting continuance in this world. ﴿أَفَإِنْ مِتَّ فَهُمُ الْخَالِدُونَ﴾ ("So if you die, will they be immortal?"): meaning, will they be the immortal ones? This is like the words of the poet:

*"They soothed me and said, 'O Khuwaylid, do not be afraid!'
I said, and the faces denied it: 'Them? Them?'"* [[Kitab al-'Ain: 8/281.]]

That is, "Are they?" This verse was revealed when they said: "We are waiting for Muhammad's (ﷺ) fate of death."

﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ﴾ ("Every soul will taste death"), meaning every created soul. ﴿وَنَبْلُوكُمْ بِالشَّرِّ وَالْخَيْرِ فِتْنَةً﴾ ("And We test you with evil and with good as a trial"): a test, to see how you give thanks for what you love and how you endure what you hate. ﴿وَإِلَيْنَا تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ ("And to Us you will be returned").

﴿وَإِذَا رَآكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِنْ يَتَّخِذُونَكَ إِلَّا هُزُوًا﴾ ("When those who disbelieve see you, they take you only as a mockery"): mocking. ﴿أَهَذَا الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ آلِهَتَكُمْ﴾ ("Is this the one who mentions your gods?") with disparagement and reproach. 'Antara said:

*"Do not mention my horse, or what I have fed him,
or your skin will be like the skin of a mangy camel."* [[Lisan al-'Arab: 4/310.]]

That is, "Do not disparage my mount."

﴿خُلِقَ الْإِنْسَانُ مِنْ عَجَلٍ﴾ ("Man was created of haste"): meaning Adam. The common reciters read *khuliqa* with a damma on the *kha'* and a kasra on the *lam* (passive). Hamid and al-A'raj read it with a fatha on both, meaning "Allah created man of haste."

Scholars differed on this. Some said: his structure and creation are of haste, and he was made with it. A parallel is His saying ﴿وَكَانَ الْإِنْسَانُ عَجُولًا﴾ ("And man has always been hasty," 17:11).

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi said: when the spirit entered the eyes of Adam, he looked at the fruits of Paradise. When it entered his body, he craved food, and he leaped before the spirit reached his feet toward the fruits of Paradise. That is the meaning of ﴿خُلِقَ الْإِنْسَانُ مِنْ عَجَلٍ﴾.

Others said: its meaning is that man was created from a hastening in Allah's creation of him. They said: He created him at the end of the day, on Friday, before sunset, and so He hastened his creation before it set.

Mujahid said: Allah created Adam after everything else, at the end of the day on which the creatures were created. When the spirit gave life to his head but had not reached his lower body, he said: "O Lord, hurry with my creation before the sun sets."

Some said: this is an inverted (*maqlub*) construction, meaning: "haste was created from man," as the Arabs say: "I presented the she-camel to the watering trough," meaning "I presented the trough to the she-camel." Also as they say: "When the Shi'ra star rises, and the wood is level with the *hurba*," meaning the *hurba* is level with the wood. Ibn Muqbil said:

*"I drew back my hand from the garment, taking it,
alone, dragged over the hands of the ransomed ones."* [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 17/37.]]

He means: "I drew the garment back from my hand." Similar examples are many.

Abu 'Ubayd said: many people of meaning say that *'ajal* means clay in the language of Himyar, and they recited:

*"The acacia grows between the rocks, bright in the sun,
and the palm grows between the water and the clay."* [[Lisan al-'Arab: 11/428. The phrase is: "and the acacia grows in the hard rock. And the palm grows between the water and the *'ajal*."]]

That is, clay.

﴿سَأُرِيكُمْ آيَاتِي فَلَا تَسْتَعْجِلُونِ﴾ ("I will show you My signs, so do not seek to hasten"): hastening the punishment and asking for signs. ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَى هَذَا الْوَعْدُ﴾ ("And they say: When is this promise?"), meaning the punishment you promise us. It is also said: the Resurrection. Its implied sense is "the promised thing." ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ ("If you are truthful").

Allah said: ﴿لَوْ يَعْلَمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا حِينَ لَا يَكُفُّونَ عَنْ وُجُوهِهِمُ النَّارَ وَلَا عَنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ﴾ ("If only those who disbelieve knew the time when they will not be able to hold back the Fire from their faces or from their backs, nor will they be helped"). *Yakuffuna* means "they will be prevented." The verse is elliptical: it means, when they persisted in their disbelief and did not repent.

﴿بَلْ تَأْتِيهِمْ بَغْتَةً﴾ ("Rather, it will come upon them suddenly"): meaning the Hour. Suddenly, unexpectedly. ﴿فَتَبْهَتُهُمْ﴾ ("and it will bewilder them"). Ibn 'Abbas said: it will surprise them. Al-Farra' said: it will confound them. ﴿فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ رَدَّهَا وَلَا هُمْ يُنْظَرُونَ﴾ ("They will not be able to avert it, nor will they be reprieved").

﴿وَلَقَدِ اسْتُهْزِئَ بِرُسُلٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ فَحَاقَ بِالَّذِينَ سَخِرُوا مِنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ﴾ ("Messengers before you were mocked, and what they used to mock befell those who scoffed at them"). ﴿قُلْ مَنْ يَكْلَؤُكُمْ بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ﴾ ("Say: Who protects you by night and day from the Most Merciful?"): that is, who guards and shields you, when His punishment descends upon you. The meaning of the verse is: from the command of the Most Merciful and His punishment.

Then He said: ﴿بَلْ هُمْ عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّهِمْ مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ ("Rather, they turn away from the remembrance of their Lord"), meaning the Book of their Lord.

﴿أَمْ لَهُمْ آلِهَةٌ تَمْنَعُهُمْ مِنْ دُونِنَا﴾ ("Or do they have gods that protect them from beside Us?"). The *mim* here and in similar places is an extension (*sila*). ﴿لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ نَصْرَ أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ ("They cannot help themselves"), so how could they help their worshippers?

﴿وَلَا هُمْ مِنَّا يُصْحَبُونَ﴾ ("Nor will they be granted companionship from Us"). Ibn 'Abbas said: they will be protected. 'Ata' related from him: they will be given protection. The Arabs say: "I am your protector and companion against so-and-so," meaning a protector against him. Mujahid said: they will be helped and preserved. Qatada said: they will not be companioned by anything good from Allah.

﴿بَلْ مَتَّعْنَا هَؤُلَاءِ﴾ ("Rather, We provided for these disbelievers and their fathers") ﴿وَآبَاءَهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيَا حَتَّى طَالَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْعُمُرُ﴾ ("in this world until their lives were prolonged"). ﴿أَفَلَا يَرَوْنَ أَنَّا نَأْتِي الْأَرْضَ نَنْقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَا﴾ ("Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its edges?"), meaning: what We diminish from the edges of the polytheists, and increase in the edges of the believers.

﴿أَفَهُمُ الْغَالِبُونَ﴾ ("Are they the victors?") or are We? ﴿قُلْ إِنَّمَا أُنْذِرُكُمْ بِالْوَحْيِ﴾ ("Say: I only warn you by revelation"), by the Qur'an. ﴿وَلَا يَسْمَعُ الصُّمُّ الدُّعَاءَ﴾ ("And the deaf do not hear the call").

Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami read *yusma'u* with a damma on the *ya'* and a fatha on the *mim*. The damma indicates the passive, in the sense that this is not done to them, according to the convention of an unnamed agent.

Ibn 'Amir read *tusma'u* with a damma on the *ta'* and a kasra on the *mim*, with *al-summu* in the accusative, making the address to the Prophet (peace be upon him). The rest read *yasma'u* with a fatha on the *ya'* and on the *mim*, with *al-summu* in the nominative, meaning the action belongs to them. ﴿إِذَا مَا يُنْذَرُونَ﴾ ("when they are warned"), meaning frightened and cautioned.

﴿وَلَئِنْ مَسَّتْهُمْ نَفْحَةٌ مِنْ عَذَابِ رَبِّكَ﴾ ("And if even a breath of your Lord's punishment touches them"). Ibn 'Abbas said: a portion. Muqatil and Qatada said: a punishment. Ibn Kaysan said: a little. Ibn Jurayj said: a share, from the saying of the Arabs: "So-and-so *nafaha* to so-and-so" when he gave him a share [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: "from his wealth."]] and a portion of it. Some said: a blow, from the Arabs' saying: "The animal *nafahat* with its leg" when it kicked with it. The poet said:

*"And a woman of the finest women,
whose sleeves are perfumed with musk."* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/293.]]

﴿لَيَقُولُنَّ يَا وَيْلَنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَالِمِينَ﴾ ("They will surely say: Woe to us! We were indeed wrongdoers").

﴿وَنَضَعُ الْمَوَازِينَ الْقِسْطَ﴾ ("And We will set up the scales of justice"), meaning the reckoning. The word *qist* (justice) is singular though *mawazin* is plural, because it is in the sense of justice and contentment.

Mujahid said: this is an image, and by the scale He means justice.

﴿فَلَا تُظْلَمُ نَفْسٌ شَيْئًا﴾ ("So no soul will be wronged in anything"): nothing is reduced from its good deeds nor added to its bad deeds.

It is reported that Dawud (peace be upon him) asked his Lord to show him the scale, and He showed it to him. When he saw it, he fainted, then recovered and said: "My God, who can fill its pan with good deeds?" He said: "O Dawud, when I am pleased with My servant, I fill it with a date."

If it is asked: how can this verse be reconciled with His saying ﴿فَلَا نُقِيمُ لَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَزْنًا﴾ ("We will not give them any weight on the Day of Resurrection," 18:105)? The answer: its meaning is: We will not weigh them (*nuqawwimuha*), and they will not be upright in truth, [the one who questioned him is the one who deficient, as in the manuscript], because they are false.

﴿وَإِنْ كَانَ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍ مِنْ خَرْدَلٍ﴾ ("Even if it is the weight of a grain of mustard seed"). The people of Medina read *mithqalu* in the nominative, meaning "even if it falls," with no predicate. The rest read it in the accusative, meaning "even if that thing is of the weight of a grain." A similar construction is in Surah Luqman: ﴿أَتَيْنَا بِهَا﴾ ("We bring it," 31:16), meaning "We bring it into account." Mujahid read *atayna* with a long vowel, meaning "We reward it." ﴿وَكَفَى بِنَا حَاسِبِينَ﴾ ("And We are sufficient as reckoners").

﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى وَهَارُونَ الْفُرْقَانَ﴾ ("We gave Musa and Harun the Criterion"), meaning the Book that distinguishes truth from falsehood, which is the Torah.

Ibn Zayd said: it is victory over enemies. The evidence is His saying ﴿وَمَا أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَى عَبْدِنَا يَوْمَ الْفُرْقَانِ﴾ ("And what We sent down to Our servant on the Day of the Criterion," 8:41), meaning the day of Badr. This view is closer to the apparent meaning of the verse, because of the waw entering on *al-diya'* [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: so the meaning of the verse is: And We gave Musa and Harun victory and the Torah, which is the light and the reminder for the God-fearing.]] and *al-dhikr* (the reminder) for the God-fearing. On this interpretation, the waw is extra and superfluous, like His saying ﴿بِزِينَةٍ الْكَوَاكِبِ وَحِفْظًا﴾ ("With an adornment of the stars, and as a protection," 37:6–7).

It is reported that 'Ikrima used to say about this verse: its meaning is: "We gave Musa and Harun the Criterion, a light." He would say: move this waw to His saying ﴿الَّذِينَ يَحْمِلُونَ الْعَرْشَ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهُ﴾ ("Those who bear the Throne and those around it," 40:7).

﴿الَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ بِالْغَيْبِ﴾ ("Those who fear their Lord unseen"), meaning they fear Him though they have not seen Him, ﴿وَهُمْ مِنَ السَّاعَةِ مُشْفِقُونَ﴾ ("and they are apprehensive of the Hour").

﴿وَهَذَا ذِكْرٌ مُبَارَكٌ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ﴾ ("And this is a blessed reminder which We have sent down"), meaning the Qur'an. ﴿أَفَأَنْتُمْ لَهُ مُنْكِرُونَ﴾ ("Will you then deny it?"), meaning: rejecting and denying.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 21, verses 30–50:

﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَ﴾ The common reciters read it with a waw (*awa lam yara*, "Have not seen"). Ibn Kathir read *a-lam yara* (without the waw), and it is written so in their codices. [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: *ya'tabiru* (they should reflect).]] ﴿...يَرَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنَّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ كَانَتَا رَتْقًا فَفَتَقْنَاهُمَا﴾ ("Have those who disbelieve not seen that the heavens and the earth were a joined mass, and We separated them?").

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Dahhak, 'Ata' and Qatada said: it means they were one thing, stuck together, and Allah separated them with air.

Ka'b said: Allah created the heavens and the earths, one upon another, then He created a wind that passed between them and split them apart with it.

Mujahid, Abu Salih and al-Suddi said: the heavens were a single joined layer, and He split them and made them seven heavens. Likewise the earths were a single joined layer, and He split them and made them seven earths.

'Ikrima, 'Ata' (*'Atiyya*) and Ibn Zayd said: the sky was a joined mass that did not rain, and the earth was a joined mass that did not produce plants. So He split the sky with rain and the earth with vegetation. A parallel to this is His saying ﴿وَالسَّمَاءِ ذَاتِ الرَّجْعِ * وَالْأَرْضِ ذَاتِ الصَّدْعِ﴾ ("By the sky that returns, and the earth that splits open," 86:11–12). The root *ratq* means a barrier or closure, and from it a woman whose vagina is sealed is called *ratq*. The root *fatq* means opening. The word *ratq*, though it describes the heavens and the earth, is in the singular because it is a verbal noun (*masdar*) placed in the position of a noun, like *al-zawr*, *al-sawm*, *al-fitr* and *al-'adl* and similar words.

﴿وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ الْمَاءِ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ حَيٍّ﴾ ("And We made from water every living thing"): this means that every living thing is created from water. A parallel is His saying ﴿وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَ كُلَّ دَابَّةٍ مِنْ مَاءٍ﴾ ("And Allah created every creature from water," 24:45).

﴿أَفَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ ("Will they not believe?"). ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا فِي الْأَرْضِ رَوَاسِيَ أَنْ تَمِيدَ بِهِمْ وَجَعَلْنَا فِيهَا فِجَاجًا سُبُلًا لَعَلَّهُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ﴾ ("And We placed firm mountains on the earth so it would not shake with them, and We made in it broad passages as roads, that they may be guided"). The words *fijaj* ("broad passages") means paths and routes; its singular is *fajj*. Then He explained it by saying *subulan* ("roads").

﴿وَجَعَلْنَا السَّمَاءَ سَقْفًا مَحْفُوظًا﴾ ("And We made the sky a protected ceiling"), protected from falling. Its evidence is His saying ﴿وَيُمْسِكُ السَّمَاءَ أَنْ تَقَعَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ﴾ ("And He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth except by His permission," 22:65). It is also said: protected from the devils, as evidenced by His saying ﴿وَحَفِظْنَاهَا مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ رَجِيمٍ﴾ ("And We guarded it from every accursed devil," 15:17).

﴿وَهُمْ عَنْ آيَاتِهَا مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ ("Yet they turn away from its signs"): they do not reflect on them or take lessons from them. This refers to the disbelievers.

﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ كُلٌّ فِي فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ﴾ ("It is He who created the night and the day, the sun and the moon; each in an orbit they float"): they move and travel. The *falak* is the orbit of the stars that contains them, and from the same root comes *falakat al-mighzal* (the whorl of a spindle).

Mujahid said: it is like the iron disc of a millstone. Al-Dahhak said: its *falak* is its path and the speed of its movement.

Others said: the *falak* is a moving, restrained wave in which the sun, moon and stars flow.

Some said: the *falak* is the sky in which that star is, and each star moves in the sky in which it was determined. This has the same meaning as Qatada's view.

﴿وَمَا جَعَلْنَا لِبَشَرٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ الْخُلْدَ﴾ ("And We did not grant immortality to any human before you"): meaning lasting continuance in this world. ﴿أَفَإِنْ مِتَّ فَهُمُ الْخَالِدُونَ﴾ ("So if you die, will they be immortal?"): meaning, will they be the immortal ones? This is like the words of the poet:

*"They soothed me and said, 'O Khuwaylid, do not be afraid!'
I said, and the faces denied it: 'Them? Them?'"* [[Kitab al-'Ain: 8/281.]]

That is, "Are they?" This verse was revealed when they said: "We are waiting for Muhammad's (ﷺ) fate of death."

﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ﴾ ("Every soul will taste death"), meaning every created soul. ﴿وَنَبْلُوكُمْ بِالشَّرِّ وَالْخَيْرِ فِتْنَةً﴾ ("And We test you with evil and with good as a trial"): a test, to see how you give thanks for what you love and how you endure what you hate. ﴿وَإِلَيْنَا تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ ("And to Us you will be returned").

﴿وَإِذَا رَآكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِنْ يَتَّخِذُونَكَ إِلَّا هُزُوًا﴾ ("When those who disbelieve see you, they take you only as a mockery"): mocking. ﴿أَهَذَا الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ آلِهَتَكُمْ﴾ ("Is this the one who mentions your gods?") with disparagement and reproach. 'Antara said:

*"Do not mention my horse, or what I have fed him,
or your skin will be like the skin of a mangy camel."* [[Lisan al-'Arab: 4/310.]]

That is, "Do not disparage my mount."

﴿خُلِقَ الْإِنْسَانُ مِنْ عَجَلٍ﴾ ("Man was created of haste"): meaning Adam. The common reciters read *khuliqa* with a damma on the *kha'* and a kasra on the *lam* (passive). Hamid and al-A'raj read it with a fatha on both, meaning "Allah created man of haste."

Scholars differed on this. Some said: his structure and creation are of haste, and he was made with it. A parallel is His saying ﴿وَكَانَ الْإِنْسَانُ عَجُولًا﴾ ("And man has always been hasty," 17:11).

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi said: when the spirit entered the eyes of Adam, he looked at the fruits of Paradise. When it entered his body, he craved food, and he leaped before the spirit reached his feet toward the fruits of Paradise. That is the meaning of ﴿خُلِقَ الْإِنْسَانُ مِنْ عَجَلٍ﴾.

Others said: its meaning is that man was created from a hastening in Allah's creation of him. They said: He created him at the end of the day, on Friday, before sunset, and so He hastened his creation before it set.

Mujahid said: Allah created Adam after everything else, at the end of the day on which the creatures were created. When the spirit gave life to his head but had not reached his lower body, he said: "O Lord, hurry with my creation before the sun sets."

Some said: this is an inverted (*maqlub*) construction, meaning: "haste was created from man," as the Arabs say: "I presented the she-camel to the watering trough," meaning "I presented the trough to the she-camel." Also as they say: "When the Shi'ra star rises, and the wood is level with the *hurba*," meaning the *hurba* is level with the wood. Ibn Muqbil said:

*"I drew back my hand from the garment, taking it,
alone, dragged over the hands of the ransomed ones."* [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 17/37.]]

He means: "I drew the garment back from my hand." Similar examples are many.

Abu 'Ubayd said: many people of meaning say that *'ajal* means clay in the language of Himyar, and they recited:

*"The acacia grows between the rocks, bright in the sun,
and the palm grows between the water and the clay."* [[Lisan al-'Arab: 11/428. The phrase is: "and the acacia grows in the hard rock. And the palm grows between the water and the *'ajal*."]]

That is, clay.

﴿سَأُرِيكُمْ آيَاتِي فَلَا تَسْتَعْجِلُونِ﴾ ("I will show you My signs, so do not seek to hasten"): hastening the punishment and asking for signs. ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَى هَذَا الْوَعْدُ﴾ ("And they say: When is this promise?"), meaning the punishment you promise us. It is also said: the Resurrection. Its implied sense is "the promised thing." ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ ("If you are truthful").

Allah said: ﴿لَوْ يَعْلَمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا حِينَ لَا يَكُفُّونَ عَنْ وُجُوهِهِمُ النَّارَ وَلَا عَنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ﴾ ("If only those who disbelieve knew the time when they will not be able to hold back the Fire from their faces or from their backs, nor will they be helped"). *Yakuffuna* means "they will be prevented." The verse is elliptical: it means, when they persisted in their disbelief and did not repent.

﴿بَلْ تَأْتِيهِمْ بَغْتَةً﴾ ("Rather, it will come upon them suddenly"): meaning the Hour. Suddenly, unexpectedly. ﴿فَتَبْهَتُهُمْ﴾ ("and it will bewilder them"). Ibn 'Abbas said: it will surprise them. Al-Farra' said: it will confound them. ﴿فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ رَدَّهَا وَلَا هُمْ يُنْظَرُونَ﴾ ("They will not be able to avert it, nor will they be reprieved").

﴿وَلَقَدِ اسْتُهْزِئَ بِرُسُلٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ فَحَاقَ بِالَّذِينَ سَخِرُوا مِنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ﴾ ("Messengers before you were mocked, and what they used to mock befell those who scoffed at them"). ﴿قُلْ مَنْ يَكْلَؤُكُمْ بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ﴾ ("Say: Who protects you by night and day from the Most Merciful?"): that is, who guards and shields you, when His punishment descends upon you. The meaning of the verse is: from the command of the Most Merciful and His punishment.

Then He said: ﴿بَلْ هُمْ عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّهِمْ مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ ("Rather, they turn away from the remembrance of their Lord"), meaning the Book of their Lord.

﴿أَمْ لَهُمْ آلِهَةٌ تَمْنَعُهُمْ مِنْ دُونِنَا﴾ ("Or do they have gods that protect them from beside Us?"). The *mim* here and in similar places is an extension (*sila*). ﴿لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ نَصْرَ أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ ("They cannot help themselves"), so how could they help their worshippers?

﴿وَلَا هُمْ مِنَّا يُصْحَبُونَ﴾ ("Nor will they be granted companionship from Us"). Ibn 'Abbas said: they will be protected. 'Ata' related from him: they will be given protection. The Arabs say: "I am your protector and companion against so-and-so," meaning a protector against him. Mujahid said: they will be helped and preserved. Qatada said: they will not be companioned by anything good from Allah.

﴿بَلْ مَتَّعْنَا هَؤُلَاءِ﴾ ("Rather, We provided for these disbelievers and their fathers") ﴿وَآبَاءَهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيَا حَتَّى طَالَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْعُمُرُ﴾ ("in this world until their lives were prolonged"). ﴿أَفَلَا يَرَوْنَ أَنَّا نَأْتِي الْأَرْضَ نَنْقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَا﴾ ("Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its edges?"), meaning: what We diminish from the edges of the polytheists, and increase in the edges of the believers.

﴿أَفَهُمُ الْغَالِبُونَ﴾ ("Are they the victors?") or are We? ﴿قُلْ إِنَّمَا أُنْذِرُكُمْ بِالْوَحْيِ﴾ ("Say: I only warn you by revelation"), by the Qur'an. ﴿وَلَا يَسْمَعُ الصُّمُّ الدُّعَاءَ﴾ ("And the deaf do not hear the call").

Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami read *yusma'u* with a damma on the *ya'* and a fatha on the *mim*. The damma indicates the passive, in the sense that this is not done to them, according to the convention of an unnamed agent.

Ibn 'Amir read *tusma'u* with a damma on the *ta'* and a kasra on the *mim*, with *al-summu* in the accusative, making the address to the Prophet (peace be upon him). The rest read *yasma'u* with a fatha on the *ya'* and on the *mim*, with *al-summu* in the nominative, meaning the action belongs to them. ﴿إِذَا مَا يُنْذَرُونَ﴾ ("when they are warned"), meaning frightened and cautioned.

﴿وَلَئِنْ مَسَّتْهُمْ نَفْحَةٌ مِنْ عَذَابِ رَبِّكَ﴾ ("And if even a breath of your Lord's punishment touches them"). Ibn 'Abbas said: a portion. Muqatil and Qatada said: a punishment. Ibn Kaysan said: a little. Ibn Jurayj said: a share, from the saying of the Arabs: "So-and-so *nafaha* to so-and-so" when he gave him a share [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: "from his wealth."]] and a portion of it. Some said: a blow, from the Arabs' saying: "The animal *nafahat* with its leg" when it kicked with it. The poet said:

*"And a woman of the finest women,
whose sleeves are perfumed with musk."* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/293.]]

﴿لَيَقُولُنَّ يَا وَيْلَنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَالِمِينَ﴾ ("They will surely say: Woe to us! We were indeed wrongdoers").

﴿وَنَضَعُ الْمَوَازِينَ الْقِسْطَ﴾ ("And We will set up the scales of justice"), meaning the reckoning. The word *qist* (justice) is singular though *mawazin* is plural, because it is in the sense of justice and contentment.

Mujahid said: this is an image, and by the scale He means justice.

﴿فَلَا تُظْلَمُ نَفْسٌ شَيْئًا﴾ ("So no soul will be wronged in anything"): nothing is reduced from its good deeds nor added to its bad deeds.

It is reported that Dawud (peace be upon him) asked his Lord to show him the scale, and He showed it to him. When he saw it, he fainted, then recovered and said: "My God, who can fill its pan with good deeds?" He said: "O Dawud, when I am pleased with My servant, I fill it with a date."

If it is asked: how can this verse be reconciled with His saying ﴿فَلَا نُقِيمُ لَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَزْنًا﴾ ("We will not give them any weight on the Day of Resurrection," 18:105)? The answer: its meaning is: We will not weigh them (*nuqawwimuha*), and they will not be upright in truth, [the one who questioned him is the one who deficient, as in the manuscript], because they are false.

﴿وَإِنْ كَانَ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍ مِنْ خَرْدَلٍ﴾ ("Even if it is the weight of a grain of mustard seed"). The people of Medina read *mithqalu* in the nominative, meaning "even if it falls," with no predicate. The rest read it in the accusative, meaning "even if that thing is of the weight of a grain." A similar construction is in Surah Luqman: ﴿أَتَيْنَا بِهَا﴾ ("We bring it," 31:16), meaning "We bring it into account." Mujahid read *atayna* with a long vowel, meaning "We reward it." ﴿وَكَفَى بِنَا حَاسِبِينَ﴾ ("And We are sufficient as reckoners").

﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى وَهَارُونَ الْفُرْقَانَ﴾ ("We gave Musa and Harun the Criterion"), meaning the Book that distinguishes truth from falsehood, which is the Torah.

Ibn Zayd said: it is victory over enemies. The evidence is His saying ﴿وَمَا أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَى عَبْدِنَا يَوْمَ الْفُرْقَانِ﴾ ("And what We sent down to Our servant on the Day of the Criterion," 8:41), meaning the day of Badr. This view is closer to the apparent meaning of the verse, because of the waw entering on *al-diya'* [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: so the meaning of the verse is: And We gave Musa and Harun victory and the Torah, which is the light and the reminder for the God-fearing.]] and *al-dhikr* (the reminder) for the God-fearing. On this interpretation, the waw is extra and superfluous, like His saying ﴿بِزِينَةٍ الْكَوَاكِبِ وَحِفْظًا﴾ ("With an adornment of the stars, and as a protection," 37:6–7).

It is reported that 'Ikrima used to say about this verse: its meaning is: "We gave Musa and Harun the Criterion, a light." He would say: move this waw to His saying ﴿الَّذِينَ يَحْمِلُونَ الْعَرْشَ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهُ﴾ ("Those who bear the Throne and those around it," 40:7).

﴿الَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ بِالْغَيْبِ﴾ ("Those who fear their Lord unseen"), meaning they fear Him though they have not seen Him, ﴿وَهُمْ مِنَ السَّاعَةِ مُشْفِقُونَ﴾ ("and they are apprehensive of the Hour").

﴿وَهَذَا ذِكْرٌ مُبَارَكٌ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ﴾ ("And this is a blessed reminder which We have sent down"), meaning the Qur'an. ﴿أَفَأَنْتُمْ لَهُ مُنْكِرُونَ﴾ ("Will you then deny it?"), meaning: rejecting and denying.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 21, verses 30–50:

﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَ﴾ The common reciters read it with a waw (*awa lam yara*, "Have not seen"). Ibn Kathir read *a-lam yara* (without the waw), and it is written so in their codices. [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: *ya'tabiru* (they should reflect).]] ﴿...يَرَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنَّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ كَانَتَا رَتْقًا فَفَتَقْنَاهُمَا﴾ ("Have those who disbelieve not seen that the heavens and the earth were a joined mass, and We separated them?").

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Dahhak, 'Ata' and Qatada said: it means they were one thing, stuck together, and Allah separated them with air.

Ka'b said: Allah created the heavens and the earths, one upon another, then He created a wind that passed between them and split them apart with it.

Mujahid, Abu Salih and al-Suddi said: the heavens were a single joined layer, and He split them and made them seven heavens. Likewise the earths were a single joined layer, and He split them and made them seven earths.

'Ikrima, 'Ata' (*'Atiyya*) and Ibn Zayd said: the sky was a joined mass that did not rain, and the earth was a joined mass that did not produce plants. So He split the sky with rain and the earth with vegetation. A parallel to this is His saying ﴿وَالسَّمَاءِ ذَاتِ الرَّجْعِ * وَالْأَرْضِ ذَاتِ الصَّدْعِ﴾ ("By the sky that returns, and the earth that splits open," 86:11–12). The root *ratq* means a barrier or closure, and from it a woman whose vagina is sealed is called *ratq*. The root *fatq* means opening. The word *ratq*, though it describes the heavens and the earth, is in the singular because it is a verbal noun (*masdar*) placed in the position of a noun, like *al-zawr*, *al-sawm*, *al-fitr* and *al-'adl* and similar words.

﴿وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ الْمَاءِ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ حَيٍّ﴾ ("And We made from water every living thing"): this means that every living thing is created from water. A parallel is His saying ﴿وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَ كُلَّ دَابَّةٍ مِنْ مَاءٍ﴾ ("And Allah created every creature from water," 24:45).

﴿أَفَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ ("Will they not believe?"). ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا فِي الْأَرْضِ رَوَاسِيَ أَنْ تَمِيدَ بِهِمْ وَجَعَلْنَا فِيهَا فِجَاجًا سُبُلًا لَعَلَّهُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ﴾ ("And We placed firm mountains on the earth so it would not shake with them, and We made in it broad passages as roads, that they may be guided"). The words *fijaj* ("broad passages") means paths and routes; its singular is *fajj*. Then He explained it by saying *subulan* ("roads").

﴿وَجَعَلْنَا السَّمَاءَ سَقْفًا مَحْفُوظًا﴾ ("And We made the sky a protected ceiling"), protected from falling. Its evidence is His saying ﴿وَيُمْسِكُ السَّمَاءَ أَنْ تَقَعَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ﴾ ("And He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth except by His permission," 22:65). It is also said: protected from the devils, as evidenced by His saying ﴿وَحَفِظْنَاهَا مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ رَجِيمٍ﴾ ("And We guarded it from every accursed devil," 15:17).

﴿وَهُمْ عَنْ آيَاتِهَا مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ ("Yet they turn away from its signs"): they do not reflect on them or take lessons from them. This refers to the disbelievers.

﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ كُلٌّ فِي فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ﴾ ("It is He who created the night and the day, the sun and the moon; each in an orbit they float"): they move and travel. The *falak* is the orbit of the stars that contains them, and from the same root comes *falakat al-mighzal* (the whorl of a spindle).

Mujahid said: it is like the iron disc of a millstone. Al-Dahhak said: its *falak* is its path and the speed of its movement.

Others said: the *falak* is a moving, restrained wave in which the sun, moon and stars flow.

Some said: the *falak* is the sky in which that star is, and each star moves in the sky in which it was determined. This has the same meaning as Qatada's view.

﴿وَمَا جَعَلْنَا لِبَشَرٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ الْخُلْدَ﴾ ("And We did not grant immortality to any human before you"): meaning lasting continuance in this world. ﴿أَفَإِنْ مِتَّ فَهُمُ الْخَالِدُونَ﴾ ("So if you die, will they be immortal?"): meaning, will they be the immortal ones? This is like the words of the poet:

*"They soothed me and said, 'O Khuwaylid, do not be afraid!'
I said, and the faces denied it: 'Them? Them?'"* [[Kitab al-'Ain: 8/281.]]

That is, "Are they?" This verse was revealed when they said: "We are waiting for Muhammad's (ﷺ) fate of death."

﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ﴾ ("Every soul will taste death"), meaning every created soul. ﴿وَنَبْلُوكُمْ بِالشَّرِّ وَالْخَيْرِ فِتْنَةً﴾ ("And We test you with evil and with good as a trial"): a test, to see how you give thanks for what you love and how you endure what you hate. ﴿وَإِلَيْنَا تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ ("And to Us you will be returned").

﴿وَإِذَا رَآكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِنْ يَتَّخِذُونَكَ إِلَّا هُزُوًا﴾ ("When those who disbelieve see you, they take you only as a mockery"): mocking. ﴿أَهَذَا الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ آلِهَتَكُمْ﴾ ("Is this the one who mentions your gods?") with disparagement and reproach. 'Antara said:

*"Do not mention my horse, or what I have fed him,
or your skin will be like the skin of a mangy camel."* [[Lisan al-'Arab: 4/310.]]

That is, "Do not disparage my mount."

﴿خُلِقَ الْإِنْسَانُ مِنْ عَجَلٍ﴾ ("Man was created of haste"): meaning Adam. The common reciters read *khuliqa* with a damma on the *kha'* and a kasra on the *lam* (passive). Hamid and al-A'raj read it with a fatha on both, meaning "Allah created man of haste."

Scholars differed on this. Some said: his structure and creation are of haste, and he was made with it. A parallel is His saying ﴿وَكَانَ الْإِنْسَانُ عَجُولًا﴾ ("And man has always been hasty," 17:11).

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi said: when the spirit entered the eyes of Adam, he looked at the fruits of Paradise. When it entered his body, he craved food, and he leaped before the spirit reached his feet toward the fruits of Paradise. That is the meaning of ﴿خُلِقَ الْإِنْسَانُ مِنْ عَجَلٍ﴾.

Others said: its meaning is that man was created from a hastening in Allah's creation of him. They said: He created him at the end of the day, on Friday, before sunset, and so He hastened his creation before it set.

Mujahid said: Allah created Adam after everything else, at the end of the day on which the creatures were created. When the spirit gave life to his head but had not reached his lower body, he said: "O Lord, hurry with my creation before the sun sets."

Some said: this is an inverted (*maqlub*) construction, meaning: "haste was created from man," as the Arabs say: "I presented the she-camel to the watering trough," meaning "I presented the trough to the she-camel." Also as they say: "When the Shi'ra star rises, and the wood is level with the *hurba*," meaning the *hurba* is level with the wood. Ibn Muqbil said:

*"I drew back my hand from the garment, taking it,
alone, dragged over the hands of the ransomed ones."* [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 17/37.]]

He means: "I drew the garment back from my hand." Similar examples are many.

Abu 'Ubayd said: many people of meaning say that *'ajal* means clay in the language of Himyar, and they recited:

*"The acacia grows between the rocks, bright in the sun,
and the palm grows between the water and the clay."* [[Lisan al-'Arab: 11/428. The phrase is: "and the acacia grows in the hard rock. And the palm grows between the water and the *'ajal*."]]

That is, clay.

﴿سَأُرِيكُمْ آيَاتِي فَلَا تَسْتَعْجِلُونِ﴾ ("I will show you My signs, so do not seek to hasten"): hastening the punishment and asking for signs. ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَى هَذَا الْوَعْدُ﴾ ("And they say: When is this promise?"), meaning the punishment you promise us. It is also said: the Resurrection. Its implied sense is "the promised thing." ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ ("If you are truthful").

Allah said: ﴿لَوْ يَعْلَمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا حِينَ لَا يَكُفُّونَ عَنْ وُجُوهِهِمُ النَّارَ وَلَا عَنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ﴾ ("If only those who disbelieve knew the time when they will not be able to hold back the Fire from their faces or from their backs, nor will they be helped"). *Yakuffuna* means "they will be prevented." The verse is elliptical: it means, when they persisted in their disbelief and did not repent.

﴿بَلْ تَأْتِيهِمْ بَغْتَةً﴾ ("Rather, it will come upon them suddenly"): meaning the Hour. Suddenly, unexpectedly. ﴿فَتَبْهَتُهُمْ﴾ ("and it will bewilder them"). Ibn 'Abbas said: it will surprise them. Al-Farra' said: it will confound them. ﴿فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ رَدَّهَا وَلَا هُمْ يُنْظَرُونَ﴾ ("They will not be able to avert it, nor will they be reprieved").

﴿وَلَقَدِ اسْتُهْزِئَ بِرُسُلٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ فَحَاقَ بِالَّذِينَ سَخِرُوا مِنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ﴾ ("Messengers before you were mocked, and what they used to mock befell those who scoffed at them"). ﴿قُلْ مَنْ يَكْلَؤُكُمْ بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ﴾ ("Say: Who protects you by night and day from the Most Merciful?"): that is, who guards and shields you, when His punishment descends upon you. The meaning of the verse is: from the command of the Most Merciful and His punishment.

Then He said: ﴿بَلْ هُمْ عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّهِمْ مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ ("Rather, they turn away from the remembrance of their Lord"), meaning the Book of their Lord.

﴿أَمْ لَهُمْ آلِهَةٌ تَمْنَعُهُمْ مِنْ دُونِنَا﴾ ("Or do they have gods that protect them from beside Us?"). The *mim* here and in similar places is an extension (*sila*). ﴿لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ نَصْرَ أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ ("They cannot help themselves"), so how could they help their worshippers?

﴿وَلَا هُمْ مِنَّا يُصْحَبُونَ﴾ ("Nor will they be granted companionship from Us"). Ibn 'Abbas said: they will be protected. 'Ata' related from him: they will be given protection. The Arabs say: "I am your protector and companion against so-and-so," meaning a protector against him. Mujahid said: they will be helped and preserved. Qatada said: they will not be companioned by anything good from Allah.

﴿بَلْ مَتَّعْنَا هَؤُلَاءِ﴾ ("Rather, We provided for these disbelievers and their fathers") ﴿وَآبَاءَهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيَا حَتَّى طَالَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْعُمُرُ﴾ ("in this world until their lives were prolonged"). ﴿أَفَلَا يَرَوْنَ أَنَّا نَأْتِي الْأَرْضَ نَنْقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَا﴾ ("Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its edges?"), meaning: what We diminish from the edges of the polytheists, and increase in the edges of the believers.

﴿أَفَهُمُ الْغَالِبُونَ﴾ ("Are they the victors?") or are We? ﴿قُلْ إِنَّمَا أُنْذِرُكُمْ بِالْوَحْيِ﴾ ("Say: I only warn you by revelation"), by the Qur'an. ﴿وَلَا يَسْمَعُ الصُّمُّ الدُّعَاءَ﴾ ("And the deaf do not hear the call").

Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami read *yusma'u* with a damma on the *ya'* and a fatha on the *mim*. The damma indicates the passive, in the sense that this is not done to them, according to the convention of an unnamed agent.

Ibn 'Amir read *tusma'u* with a damma on the *ta'* and a kasra on the *mim*, with *al-summu* in the accusative, making the address to the Prophet (peace be upon him). The rest read *yasma'u* with a fatha on the *ya'* and on the *mim*, with *al-summu* in the nominative, meaning the action belongs to them. ﴿إِذَا مَا يُنْذَرُونَ﴾ ("when they are warned"), meaning frightened and cautioned.

﴿وَلَئِنْ مَسَّتْهُمْ نَفْحَةٌ مِنْ عَذَابِ رَبِّكَ﴾ ("And if even a breath of your Lord's punishment touches them"). Ibn 'Abbas said: a portion. Muqatil and Qatada said: a punishment. Ibn Kaysan said: a little. Ibn Jurayj said: a share, from the saying of the Arabs: "So-and-so *nafaha* to so-and-so" when he gave him a share [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: "from his wealth."]] and a portion of it. Some said: a blow, from the Arabs' saying: "The animal *nafahat* with its leg" when it kicked with it. The poet said:

*"And a woman of the finest women,
whose sleeves are perfumed with musk."* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/293.]]

﴿لَيَقُولُنَّ يَا وَيْلَنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَالِمِينَ﴾ ("They will surely say: Woe to us! We were indeed wrongdoers").

﴿وَنَضَعُ الْمَوَازِينَ الْقِسْطَ﴾ ("And We will set up the scales of justice"), meaning the reckoning. The word *qist* (justice) is singular though *mawazin* is plural, because it is in the sense of justice and contentment.

Mujahid said: this is an image, and by the scale He means justice.

﴿فَلَا تُظْلَمُ نَفْسٌ شَيْئًا﴾ ("So no soul will be wronged in anything"): nothing is reduced from its good deeds nor added to its bad deeds.

It is reported that Dawud (peace be upon him) asked his Lord to show him the scale, and He showed it to him. When he saw it, he fainted, then recovered and said: "My God, who can fill its pan with good deeds?" He said: "O Dawud, when I am pleased with My servant, I fill it with a date."

If it is asked: how can this verse be reconciled with His saying ﴿فَلَا نُقِيمُ لَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَزْنًا﴾ ("We will not give them any weight on the Day of Resurrection," 18:105)? The answer: its meaning is: We will not weigh them (*nuqawwimuha*), and they will not be upright in truth, [the one who questioned him is the one who deficient, as in the manuscript], because they are false.

﴿وَإِنْ كَانَ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍ مِنْ خَرْدَلٍ﴾ ("Even if it is the weight of a grain of mustard seed"). The people of Medina read *mithqalu* in the nominative, meaning "even if it falls," with no predicate. The rest read it in the accusative, meaning "even if that thing is of the weight of a grain." A similar construction is in Surah Luqman: ﴿أَتَيْنَا بِهَا﴾ ("We bring it," 31:16), meaning "We bring it into account." Mujahid read *atayna* with a long vowel, meaning "We reward it." ﴿وَكَفَى بِنَا حَاسِبِينَ﴾ ("And We are sufficient as reckoners").

﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى وَهَارُونَ الْفُرْقَانَ﴾ ("We gave Musa and Harun the Criterion"), meaning the Book that distinguishes truth from falsehood, which is the Torah.

Ibn Zayd said: it is victory over enemies. The evidence is His saying ﴿وَمَا أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَى عَبْدِنَا يَوْمَ الْفُرْقَانِ﴾ ("And what We sent down to Our servant on the Day of the Criterion," 8:41), meaning the day of Badr. This view is closer to the apparent meaning of the verse, because of the waw entering on *al-diya'* [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: so the meaning of the verse is: And We gave Musa and Harun victory and the Torah, which is the light and the reminder for the God-fearing.]] and *al-dhikr* (the reminder) for the God-fearing. On this interpretation, the waw is extra and superfluous, like His saying ﴿بِزِينَةٍ الْكَوَاكِبِ وَحِفْظًا﴾ ("With an adornment of the stars, and as a protection," 37:6–7).

It is reported that 'Ikrima used to say about this verse: its meaning is: "We gave Musa and Harun the Criterion, a light." He would say: move this waw to His saying ﴿الَّذِينَ يَحْمِلُونَ الْعَرْشَ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهُ﴾ ("Those who bear the Throne and those around it," 40:7).

﴿الَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ بِالْغَيْبِ﴾ ("Those who fear their Lord unseen"), meaning they fear Him though they have not seen Him, ﴿وَهُمْ مِنَ السَّاعَةِ مُشْفِقُونَ﴾ ("and they are apprehensive of the Hour").

﴿وَهَذَا ذِكْرٌ مُبَارَكٌ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ﴾ ("And this is a blessed reminder which We have sent down"), meaning the Qur'an. ﴿أَفَأَنْتُمْ لَهُ مُنْكِرُونَ﴾ ("Will you then deny it?"), meaning: rejecting and denying.

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Dahhak, 'Ata' and Qatada said: it means they were one thing, stuck together, and Allah separated them with air.

Ka'b said: Allah created the heavens and the earths, one upon another, then He created a wind that passed between them and split them apart with it.

Mujahid, Abu Salih and al-Suddi said: the heavens were a single joined layer, and He split them and made them seven heavens. Likewise the earths were a single joined layer, and He split them and made them seven earths.

'Ikrima, 'Ata' (*'Atiyya*) and Ibn Zayd said: the sky was a joined mass that did not rain, and the earth was a joined mass that did not produce plants. So He split the sky with rain and the earth with vegetation. A parallel to this is His saying ﴿وَالسَّمَاءِ ذَاتِ الرَّجْعِ * وَالْأَرْضِ ذَاتِ الصَّدْعِ﴾ ("By the sky that returns, and the earth that splits open," 86:11–12). The root *ratq* means a barrier or closure, and from it a woman whose vagina is sealed is called *ratq*. The root *fatq* means opening. The word *ratq*, though it describes the heavens and the earth, is in the singular because it is a verbal noun (*masdar*) placed in the position of a noun, like *al-zawr*, *al-sawm*, *al-fitr* and *al-'adl* and similar words.

﴿وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ الْمَاءِ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ حَيٍّ﴾ ("And We made from water every living thing"): this means that every living thing is created from water. A parallel is His saying ﴿وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَ كُلَّ دَابَّةٍ مِنْ مَاءٍ﴾ ("And Allah created every creature from water," 24:45).

﴿أَفَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ ("Will they not believe?"). ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا فِي الْأَرْضِ رَوَاسِيَ أَنْ تَمِيدَ بِهِمْ وَجَعَلْنَا فِيهَا فِجَاجًا سُبُلًا لَعَلَّهُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ﴾ ("And We placed firm mountains on the earth so it would not shake with them, and We made in it broad passages as roads, that they may be guided"). The words *fijaj* ("broad passages") means paths and routes; its singular is *fajj*. Then He explained it by saying *subulan* ("roads").

﴿وَجَعَلْنَا السَّمَاءَ سَقْفًا مَحْفُوظًا﴾ ("And We made the sky a protected ceiling"), protected from falling. Its evidence is His saying ﴿وَيُمْسِكُ السَّمَاءَ أَنْ تَقَعَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ﴾ ("And He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth except by His permission," 22:65). It is also said: protected from the devils, as evidenced by His saying ﴿وَحَفِظْنَاهَا مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ رَجِيمٍ﴾ ("And We guarded it from every accursed devil," 15:17).

﴿وَهُمْ عَنْ آيَاتِهَا مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ ("Yet they turn away from its signs"): they do not reflect on them or take lessons from them. This refers to the disbelievers.

﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ كُلٌّ فِي فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ﴾ ("It is He who created the night and the day, the sun and the moon; each in an orbit they float"): they move and travel. The *falak* is the orbit of the stars that contains them, and from the same root comes *falakat al-mighzal* (the whorl of a spindle).

Mujahid said: it is like the iron disc of a millstone. Al-Dahhak said: its *falak* is its path and the speed of its movement.

Others said: the *falak* is a moving, restrained wave in which the sun, moon and stars flow.
