Then they were overturned upon their heads, bewildered and perplexed, and they knew that the idols do not speak nor strike. They said: ﴿You know well that these do not speak.﴾ When the proof turned against them, Abraham said to them: ﴿Do you worship besides Allah what neither benefits you at all nor harms you? Uff to you and to what you worship besides Allah! Will you not reason?﴾ When the proof was binding upon them and they were unable to answer, they said: ﴿Burn him and support your gods, if you are going to act.﴾

Ibn Umar [in the Isfahan copy: Abu Umar] said: The one who advised them to burn Abraham was a man from the Kurds. Shu'ayb al-Jubba'i said: his name was Haizan, and Allah caused the earth to swallow him, and he will keep sinking into it until the Day of Resurrection. They said: When Nimrod gathered his people to burn Abraham, they imprisoned him in a house and built a structure like an enclosure. This is His saying: ﴿They said: Build for him a structure and throw him into the blazing fire﴾ [al-Saffat: 97]. Then they gathered for him hard firewood of various kinds, so much that a woman who fell ill would say: "If he restores my health, I will surely gather firewood for Abraham." A woman would vow, in some matter she sought and loved to attain, that if it came to pass she would gather firewood for the fire of Abraham, by which he would be burned, as an act of devotion in her religion.

Ibn Ishaq said: They gathered firewood for a month. They said: Until, when they had gathered as much as they wanted, they lit fire at every side of the wood, and the fire blazed and grew so intense that a bird passing by would be burned from its intense heat. Then they went to Abraham, lifted him to the top of the structure, and bound him. Then they made a catapult and placed him in it, shackled and chained. The heavens and the earth, and whoever is in them of the angels and all creation except the two jinn and humans, cried out with one cry: "O our Lord, Abraham is not on Your earth anyone who worships You besides him, and he is to be burned for You. So permit us to help him." Allah, glorified and exalted, said to them: "If he calls upon any of you for help, let him help him, for I have permitted him in that. If he calls upon none but Me, then I know him best, and I am his protector. So leave him to Me." When they wanted to throw him into the fire, the keeper of the waters came to him and said: "If you wish, I will extinguish the fire, for the treasures of the rains are in my hand." The keeper of the winds came to him and said: "If you wish, I will scatter the fire into the air." Abraham said: "I have no need of you." Then he raised his head to the sky and said: "O Allah, You are the One in the heavens, and I am the one on the earth; there is no one on the earth who worships You besides me. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs."

Al-Mu'tamir narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from Arqam, that Abraham said when they bound him to throw him into the fire: "There is no god but You, glory be to You, Lord of the worlds; to You is praise and to You is dominion; You have no partner." He said: Then they threw him from a great distance into the fire by catapult, and Gabriel met him and said: "O Abraham, do you have any need?" He said: "As for you, no." Gabriel said: "Then ask your Lord." Abraham said: "My knowledge of my condition is sufficient for my request." Then Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿O fire, be cool and safe for Abraham.﴾ Al-Suddi said: Gabriel was the one who called to it.

Ibn Abbas said: If its coolness had not been followed by "safety," Abraham would have died from its cold. Thus no fire remained that day on earth but was extinguished, thinking that it was meant by this.

Al-Suddi said: The angels took Abraham by his armpits and seated him on the ground, and there was a spring of sweet water, a red flower, and narcissus.

Ka'b said: The fire burned nothing of Abraham except his bonds. They said: Abraham remained in that place for seven days.

Al-Minhal ibn Amr said: Abraham, the friend of Allah, said: "I never had days more pleasant than the days I spent in the fire."

Ibn Yasar said: Allah, whose name is majestic, sent the angel of shade in the form of Abraham, and he sat in the fire beside Abraham, keeping him company. They said: Allah sent him a shirt of silk from Paradise, and Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to him and said: "O Abraham, your Lord says: Did you not know that fire does not harm My beloved?" Then Nimrod looked out from a palace he had, and overlooked Abraham, and had no doubt of his death. He saw Abraham sitting in a garden, and saw the angel sitting beside him, and around him was fire burning what they had gathered of firewood. Nimrod called out: "O Abraham, is your God great, whose power has reached the point that He has prevented between you and what I see, so it did not harm you? O Abraham, can you come out of it?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Do you fear that if you remain in it, it will harm you?" He said: "No." He said: "Then get up and come out of it." Abraham got up walking in it until he came out of it. When he came out to him, he said: "O Abraham, who is the man I saw with you, sitting beside you, resembling your form?" He said: "That is the angel of shade, whom my Lord sent to keep me company in it." Nimrod said: "O Abraham, I will offer a sacrifice to your God, because of what I saw of His power and might in what He did for you, when you refused anything but His worship and His unity. I will slaughter for Him four thousand cows." Abraham said to him: "Then Allah will not accept from you while you remain on this religion of yours, until you leave it for my religion." He said: "O Abraham, I cannot leave my kingship, but I will slaughter them for Him." So Nimrod slaughtered them for Him. Then he withheld from Abraham, and Allah, glorified is He, protected him from him.

Abu Hurayrah said: The best thing Abraham said, when the covering was lifted from him while he was in the fire and his forehead was sweating, was: Nimrod said at that: "Excellent is your Lord, O Abraham." Ka'b, Qatadah and al-Zuhri said: No one among the people of the earth benefited that day from the fire, and the fire burned nothing that day except Abraham's bonds, and no creature came that day but it extinguished the fire from him, except the gecko (al-wazagh). For this reason the Prophet ﷺ commanded its killing and named it "fuwaysiq" (the mischievous little one).

Shu'ayb al-Jubba'i said: Abraham (peace be upon him) was thrown into the fire when he was sixteen years old; Isaac was sacrificed when he was seven years old; Sarah bore him when she was ninety years old; and his place of sacrifice was from the House of Iliya, two miles away. When Sarah learned what he intended with Isaac, she wailed that day and died on the third day.

Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿And they intended a scheme against him, but We made them the greatest losers.﴾ ﴿And We delivered him and Lot to the land which We had blessed for the worlds﴾, meaning from Nimrod and his people, from the land of Iraq, to the land, meaning Syria.

Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: He called it blessed because there is no sweet water but that its source springs from under the rock that is in Bayt al-Maqdis.

Qatadah said: It was said: Syria is the outskirts of the abode of emigration; what is lacking from the land is added to Syria, and what is lacking from Syria is added to Palestine. It was said: It is the land of the gathering and the resurrection, the place where people assemble, where Jesus son of Mary will descend, and where Allah will destroy the Dajjal.

Abu Qilabah narrated that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "I saw in a dream as if the angels carried the pillar of the Book and placed it in Syria. I interpreted that when trials occur, faith is in Syria."

It has been mentioned to us that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said to Ka'b: "Would you not move to Medina, for it is the place of emigration of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the site of his grave?" Ka'b said to him: "O Commander of the Faithful, I find in the revealed Book of Allah that Syria is the treasure of Allah from His earth, and there is His treasure from His servants."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said: Some men of his people responded to Abraham when they saw what Allah, glorified is He, had done to him, making the fire ﴿cool and safe﴾, in fear of Nimrod and his chiefs. ﴿Lot believed in him﴾; he was his nephew, Lot son of Haran son of Terah. Haran was the brother of Abraham, and he had a third brother called Bahur son of Terah. Haran was the father of Lot; Nahur was the father of Tabwil; Tabwil was the father of Lan; and Ratqa, daughter of Tabwil, was the wife of Isaac son of Abraham, mother of Jacob; Liya and Zajil, the two daughters of Layan, were the wives of Jacob. Sarah also believed in him; she was the daughter of his paternal uncle, Sarah daughter of Haran the elder, paternal uncle of Abraham, peace be upon him.

Al-Suddi said: Sarah was the daughter of the king of Harran. Abraham and Lot set out toward Syria, and Abraham met Sarah, who was the daughter of the king of Harran, and she had criticized her people for their religion; Abraham married her on condition that he would change her.

Ibn Ishaq said: Abraham left Kuthā in the land of Iraq as an emigrant to his Lord, and Lot and Sarah went out with him, as Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿Lot believed in him, and [Abraham] said: Indeed I am emigrating to my Lord﴾. He went out seeking refuge for his religion and security for the worship of Allah, until he settled in Harran and remained there as long as Allah willed. Then he left it as an emigrant until he came to Egypt, then left Egypt for Syria and settled in al-Sab' in the land of Palestine, which is the desert of Syria. Lot settled at al-Mu'tafikah, which is one day and night's journey or a little more from al-Sab', and Allah, glorified is He, sent him as a prophet. This is His saying: ﴿And We delivered him and Lot to the land which We had blessed for the worlds﴾, meaning Syria. Its blessing is that most of the prophets were sent from it; it is a fertile land abounding in trees, rivers, and fruits, where the life of the poor and the rich is pleasant.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿to the land which We had blessed for the worlds﴾: he said: it means Mecca and the settling of Ishmael. Do you not see that He says: ﴿Indeed, the first House established for mankind is that at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for the worlds﴾ [Al 'Imran: 96]? But the first opinion is more correct.

﴿And We gave him Isaac and Jacob as an additional gift (nafilah)﴾, meaning a gift; from Mujahid. Al-Hasan and al-Dahhak said: an extra favor. Ibn Abbas, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Ibn Zayd and Qatadah said: He asked for one, saying: ﴿My Lord, grant me of the righteous﴾, so Allah gave him Isaac as a son, and increased him with Jacob, a grandson, and that is the nafilah. Mujahid and Ata' said: the meaning of nafilah is gift, and both were from the bounty of Allah, glorified is He, Who gave them to him.

﴿And We made all of them righteous﴾, meaning Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, peace be upon them.

And We had certainly given Abraham his right judgment (rushdahu), meaning his tawfiq (divine enabling). Al-Qurazi said: his righteousness, from before (min qablu), meaning before Moses and Aaron.

The exegetes said: That is, We guided him while he was young, as He said regarding Yahya: ﴿And We gave him judgment while still a boy﴾ [Maryam: 12].

And We had knowledge of him, that he was one fit for guidance and prophethood.

When he said to his father and his people: ﴿What are these statues and images to which you are devoted?﴾ That is, the idols that you are devoted to, persisting in their worship.

They said: ﴿We found our fathers worshipping them﴾, so we follow them.

He said: ﴿Indeed you and your fathers have been in clear error﴾ by your worship of them.

They said: ﴿Have you brought us the truth, or are you among the jesters?﴾ meaning: Are you serious in what you say, or are you joking?

He said: ﴿Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who created them (fatarahunna)﴾, meaning, who created them; ﴿and I am among the witnesses to that. And by Allah, I will surely plot against your idols after you have turned away, retreating﴾, meaning, I will surely scheme against them.

Mujahid and Qatadah said: Abraham said this secretly among his people, and only one man among them heard it, and he is the one who disclosed it, saying: ﴿We heard a youth mention them, called Abraham﴾.

Al-Suddi said: They had a yearly assembly and festival. Whenever they returned from their festival, they would enter upon the idols and prostrate to them, then return to their homes. When that festival came, Abraham's father said to him: "O Abraham, if you came out with us to our festival, our religion would please you." So Abraham went out with them. When he was on part of the road, he threw himself down and said: ﴿Indeed, I am sick﴾, meaning: "I am complaining of my leg." So they left him, and he lay there prostrate. When they had gone, he called out after the last of them, when only a few people remained: ﴿By Allah, I will surely plot against your idols after you have turned away, retreating﴾, and they heard it from him. Then Abraham returned to the gods, and found them in a great hall, facing the door of the hall was a great idol, and beside it smaller ones, one beside another, each idol next to it smaller than it, down to the door of the hall. They had placed food before the idols and said: "When we return, the gods will have blessed our food, and we will eat it." When Abraham looked at them and at the food before them, he said to them in mockery: ﴿Will you not eat?﴾ When none of them answered, he said: ﴿What is wrong with you that you do not speak?﴾ Then he turned upon them, striking them with his right hand, and began to break them with an axe in his hand, until only the largest idol [in the Isfahan copy: "the greatest" instead of "the largest"] remained; he hung the axe around its neck and went out. This is His saying: ﴿So he made them into fragments﴾.

Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash and al-Kisa'i read it with a kasra on the jim, meaning fragments and pieces, plural of judhadh, which is dry crumbled stalk, like khafif and khiffaf, karim and kiram. The rest read it with a damma, meaning debris and fine fragments. ﴿Except a great one among them﴾, meaning the largest of the gods, for he did not break it, and placed the axe on its neck. ﴿So that they might return to it﴾, so that they would reflect and know its weakness and powerlessness. It was also said: ﴿So that they might return to it﴾ and ask it.

When the people came back from their festival to the house of their gods and saw their idols, they said: ﴿Who has done this to our gods? Indeed, he is among the wrongdoers.﴾ They said, meaning those who had heard Abraham say: ﴿By Allah, I will surely plot against your idols﴾ ... ﴿We heard a youth mention them﴾, disparaging them, reviling them, and mocking them, ﴿called Abraham﴾: he is the one who did this. The news reached Nimrod the tyrant and the nobles of his people, and they said: ﴿Bring him before the eyes of the people﴾, meaning, in the sight of the people [in the Isfahan copy: It was said: it means "before the heads of the people"; and it was said it means "in their view"; they intended by this "in plain view", and the one who did it is for the people, as the Arabs say when a matter is made public and widespread: "That happened before the eyes of the people"], ﴿so that they may bear witness against him that he is the one who did that﴾, and they disliked taking him without evidence. This was said by Qatadah and al-Suddi.

Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: ﴿So that they may witness what is done to him and what punishment he receives﴾, that is, that they may be present. When they brought him, they said: ﴿Did you do this to our gods, O Abraham?﴾ Abraham said: ﴿Rather, it was done by this, their chief; so ask them, if they can speak.﴾ This is a rebuke over their worship of these small ones alongside this great one, which is greater than them, so he broke them. This was said by Ibn Ishaq, and Abraham intended by it to establish proof against them, which is the meaning of His saying: ﴿So ask them, if they can speak﴾, until they inform you who did this to them.

It is narrated from al-Kisa'i that he would pause at His saying "Rather, it was done by" and say: its meaning is "it was done by the one who did it", then start again with "this, their chief".

Al-Qutaybi said: Abraham made speech a condition for the act, saying: ﴿It was done by this, their chief; so ask them if they can speak﴾, and the meaning is: if they are able to act. He showed them their inability to speak and act. Implicit in this is: "I did that." What the reports agree upon regarding this verse is the saying of Ibn Ishaq, which indicates it.

The saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Abraham did not lie except three lies, all of them concerning Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: his saying ﴿I am sick﴾ [al-Saffat: 89], his saying ﴿Rather, it was done by this, their chief﴾, and his saying to Sarah: 'She is my sister.'"

It is not impossible that Allah, glorified is He, permitted His messenger and close friend to do this, in order to shame his people, rebuke them, argue against them, and make known to them the place of their error, just as He permitted it for Joseph when he commanded his crier who said to his brothers: ﴿O caravan, indeed you are thieves﴾ [Yusuf: 70], though they had not stolen anything.

﴿So they returned to themselves﴾: meaning they reflected in their hearts and returned to their minds, and they said: ﴿You have indeed wronged yourselves﴾ by asking him, since this is your gods, and what was done to them is evident, so ask them. It was also said: ﴿You are indeed the wrongdoers﴾ by your worship of small idols alongside this great one.

Then they were overturned upon their heads, bewildered and perplexed, and they knew that the idols do not speak nor strike. They said: ﴿You know well that these do not speak.﴾ When the proof turned against them, Abraham said to them: ﴿Do you worship besides Allah what neither benefits you at all nor harms you? Uff to you and to what you worship besides Allah! Will you not reason?﴾ When the proof was binding upon them and they were unable to answer, they said: ﴿Burn him and support your gods, if you are going to act.﴾

Ibn Umar [in the Isfahan copy: Abu Umar] said: The one who advised them to burn Abraham was a man from the Kurds. Shu'ayb al-Jubba'i said: his name was Haizan, and Allah caused the earth to swallow him, and he will keep sinking into it until the Day of Resurrection. They said: When Nimrod gathered his people to burn Abraham, they imprisoned him in a house and built a structure like an enclosure. This is His saying: ﴿They said: Build for him a structure and throw him into the blazing fire﴾ [al-Saffat: 97]. Then they gathered for him hard firewood of various kinds, so much that a woman who fell ill would say: "If he restores my health, I will surely gather firewood for Abraham." A woman would vow, in some matter she sought and loved to attain, that if it came to pass she would gather firewood for the fire of Abraham, by which he would be burned, as an act of devotion in her religion.

Ibn Ishaq said: They gathered firewood for a month. They said: Until, when they had gathered as much as they wanted, they lit fire at every side of the wood, and the fire blazed and grew so intense that a bird passing by would be burned from its intense heat. Then they went to Abraham, lifted him to the top of the structure, and bound him. Then they made a catapult and placed him in it, shackled and chained. The heavens and the earth, and whoever is in them of the angels and all creation except the two jinn and humans, cried out with one cry: "O our Lord, Abraham is not on Your earth anyone who worships You besides him, and he is to be burned for You. So permit us to help him." Allah, glorified and exalted, said to them: "If he calls upon any of you for help, let him help him, for I have permitted him in that. If he calls upon none but Me, then I know him best, and I am his protector. So leave him to Me." When they wanted to throw him into the fire, the keeper of the waters came to him and said: "If you wish, I will extinguish the fire, for the treasures of the rains are in my hand." The keeper of the winds came to him and said: "If you wish, I will scatter the fire into the air." Abraham said: "I have no need of you." Then he raised his head to the sky and said: "O Allah, You are the One in the heavens, and I am the one on the earth; there is no one on the earth who worships You besides me. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs."

Al-Mu'tamir narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from Arqam, that Abraham said when they bound him to throw him into the fire: "There is no god but You, glory be to You, Lord of the worlds; to You is praise and to You is dominion; You have no partner." He said: Then they threw him from a great distance into the fire by catapult, and Gabriel met him and said: "O Abraham, do you have any need?" He said: "As for you, no." Gabriel said: "Then ask your Lord." Abraham said: "My knowledge of my condition is sufficient for my request." Then Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿O fire, be cool and safe for Abraham.﴾ Al-Suddi said: Gabriel was the one who called to it.

Ibn Abbas said: If its coolness had not been followed by "safety," Abraham would have died from its cold. Thus no fire remained that day on earth but was extinguished, thinking that it was meant by this.

Al-Suddi said: The angels took Abraham by his armpits and seated him on the ground, and there was a spring of sweet water, a red flower, and narcissus.

Ka'b said: The fire burned nothing of Abraham except his bonds. They said: Abraham remained in that place for seven days.

Al-Minhal ibn Amr said: Abraham, the friend of Allah, said: "I never had days more pleasant than the days I spent in the fire."

Ibn Yasar said: Allah, whose name is majestic, sent the angel of shade in the form of Abraham, and he sat in the fire beside Abraham, keeping him company. They said: Allah sent him a shirt of silk from Paradise, and Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to him and said: "O Abraham, your Lord says: Did you not know that fire does not harm My beloved?" Then Nimrod looked out from a palace he had, and overlooked Abraham, and had no doubt of his death. He saw Abraham sitting in a garden, and saw the angel sitting beside him, and around him was fire burning what they had gathered of firewood. Nimrod called out: "O Abraham, is your God great, whose power has reached the point that He has prevented between you and what I see, so it did not harm you? O Abraham, can you come out of it?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Do you fear that if you remain in it, it will harm you?" He said: "No." He said: "Then get up and come out of it." Abraham got up walking in it until he came out of it. When he came out to him, he said: "O Abraham, who is the man I saw with you, sitting beside you, resembling your form?" He said: "That is the angel of shade, whom my Lord sent to keep me company in it." Nimrod said: "O Abraham, I will offer a sacrifice to your God, because of what I saw of His power and might in what He did for you, when you refused anything but His worship and His unity. I will slaughter for Him four thousand cows." Abraham said to him: "Then Allah will not accept from you while you remain on this religion of yours, until you leave it for my religion." He said: "O Abraham, I cannot leave my kingship, but I will slaughter them for Him." So Nimrod slaughtered them for Him. Then he withheld from Abraham, and Allah, glorified is He, protected him from him.

Abu Hurayrah said: The best thing Abraham said, when the covering was lifted from him while he was in the fire and his forehead was sweating, was: Nimrod said at that: "Excellent is your Lord, O Abraham." Ka'b, Qatadah and al-Zuhri said: No one among the people of the earth benefited that day from the fire, and the fire burned nothing that day except Abraham's bonds, and no creature came that day but it extinguished the fire from him, except the gecko (al-wazagh). For this reason the Prophet ﷺ commanded its killing and named it "fuwaysiq" (the mischievous little one).

Shu'ayb al-Jubba'i said: Abraham (peace be upon him) was thrown into the fire when he was sixteen years old; Isaac was sacrificed when he was seven years old; Sarah bore him when she was ninety years old; and his place of sacrifice was from the House of Iliya, two miles away. When Sarah learned what he intended with Isaac, she wailed that day and died on the third day.

Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿And they intended a scheme against him, but We made them the greatest losers.﴾ ﴿And We delivered him and Lot to the land which We had blessed for the worlds﴾, meaning from Nimrod and his people, from the land of Iraq, to the land, meaning Syria.

Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: He called it blessed because there is no sweet water but that its source springs from under the rock that is in Bayt al-Maqdis.

Qatadah said: It was said: Syria is the outskirts of the abode of emigration; what is lacking from the land is added to Syria, and what is lacking from Syria is added to Palestine. It was said: It is the land of the gathering and the resurrection, the place where people assemble, where Jesus son of Mary will descend, and where Allah will destroy the Dajjal.

Abu Qilabah narrated that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "I saw in a dream as if the angels carried the pillar of the Book and placed it in Syria. I interpreted that when trials occur, faith is in Syria."

It has been mentioned to us that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said to Ka'b: "Would you not move to Medina, for it is the place of emigration of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the site of his grave?" Ka'b said to him: "O Commander of the Faithful, I find in the revealed Book of Allah that Syria is the treasure of Allah from His earth, and there is His treasure from His servants."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said: Some men of his people responded to Abraham when they saw what Allah, glorified is He, had done to him, making the fire ﴿cool and safe﴾, in fear of Nimrod and his chiefs. ﴿Lot believed in him﴾; he was his nephew, Lot son of Haran son of Terah. Haran was the brother of Abraham, and he had a third brother called Bahur son of Terah. Haran was the father of Lot; Nahur was the father of Tabwil; Tabwil was the father of Lan; and Ratqa, daughter of Tabwil, was the wife of Isaac son of Abraham, mother of Jacob; Liya and Zajil, the two daughters of Layan, were the wives of Jacob. Sarah also believed in him; she was the daughter of his paternal uncle, Sarah daughter of Haran the elder, paternal uncle of Abraham, peace be upon him.

Al-Suddi said: Sarah was the daughter of the king of Harran. Abraham and Lot set out toward Syria, and Abraham met Sarah, who was the daughter of the king of Harran, and she had criticized her people for their religion; Abraham married her on condition that he would change her.

Ibn Ishaq said: Abraham left Kuthā in the land of Iraq as an emigrant to his Lord, and Lot and Sarah went out with him, as Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿Lot believed in him, and [Abraham] said: Indeed I am emigrating to my Lord﴾. He went out seeking refuge for his religion and security for the worship of Allah, until he settled in Harran and remained there as long as Allah willed. Then he left it as an emigrant until he came to Egypt, then left Egypt for Syria and settled in al-Sab' in the land of Palestine, which is the desert of Syria. Lot settled at al-Mu'tafikah, which is one day and night's journey or a little more from al-Sab', and Allah, glorified is He, sent him as a prophet. This is His saying: ﴿And We delivered him and Lot to the land which We had blessed for the worlds﴾, meaning Syria. Its blessing is that most of the prophets were sent from it; it is a fertile land abounding in trees, rivers, and fruits, where the life of the poor and the rich is pleasant.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿to the land which We had blessed for the worlds﴾: he said: it means Mecca and the settling of Ishmael. Do you not see that He says: ﴿Indeed, the first House established for mankind is that at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for the worlds﴾ [Al 'Imran: 96]? But the first opinion is more correct.

﴿And We gave him Isaac and Jacob as an additional gift (nafilah)﴾, meaning a gift; from Mujahid. Al-Hasan and al-Dahhak said: an extra favor. Ibn Abbas, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Ibn Zayd and Qatadah said: He asked for one, saying: ﴿My Lord, grant me of the righteous﴾, so Allah gave him Isaac as a son, and increased him with Jacob, a grandson, and that is the nafilah. Mujahid and Ata' said: the meaning of nafilah is gift, and both were from the bounty of Allah, glorified is He, Who gave them to him.

﴿And We made all of them righteous﴾, meaning Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, peace be upon them.

And We had certainly given Abraham his right judgment (rushdahu), meaning his tawfiq (divine enabling). Al-Qurazi said: his righteousness, from before (min qablu), meaning before Moses and Aaron.

The exegetes said: That is, We guided him while he was young, as He said regarding Yahya: ﴿And We gave him judgment while still a boy﴾ [Maryam: 12].

And We had knowledge of him, that he was one fit for guidance and prophethood.

When he said to his father and his people: ﴿What are these statues and images to which you are devoted?﴾ That is, the idols that you are devoted to, persisting in their worship.

They said: ﴿We found our fathers worshipping them﴾, so we follow them.

He said: ﴿Indeed you and your fathers have been in clear error﴾ by your worship of them.

They said: ﴿Have you brought us the truth, or are you among the jesters?﴾ meaning: Are you serious in what you say, or are you joking?

He said: ﴿Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who created them (fatarahunna)﴾, meaning, who created them; ﴿and I am among the witnesses to that. And by Allah, I will surely plot against your idols after you have turned away, retreating﴾, meaning, I will surely scheme against them.

Mujahid and Qatadah said: Abraham said this secretly among his people, and only one man among them heard it, and he is the one who disclosed it, saying: ﴿We heard a youth mention them, called Abraham﴾.

Al-Suddi said: They had a yearly assembly and festival. Whenever they returned from their festival, they would enter upon the idols and prostrate to them, then return to their homes. When that festival came, Abraham's father said to him: "O Abraham, if you came out with us to our festival, our religion would please you." So Abraham went out with them. When he was on part of the road, he threw himself down and said: ﴿Indeed, I am sick﴾, meaning: "I am complaining of my leg." So they left him, and he lay there prostrate. When they had gone, he called out after the last of them, when only a few people remained: ﴿By Allah, I will surely plot against your idols after you have turned away, retreating﴾, and they heard it from him. Then Abraham returned to the gods, and found them in a great hall, facing the door of the hall was a great idol, and beside it smaller ones, one beside another, each idol next to it smaller than it, down to the door of the hall. They had placed food before the idols and said: "When we return, the gods will have blessed our food, and we will eat it." When Abraham looked at them and at the food before them, he said to them in mockery: ﴿Will you not eat?﴾ When none of them answered, he said: ﴿What is wrong with you that you do not speak?﴾ Then he turned upon them, striking them with his right hand, and began to break them with an axe in his hand, until only the largest idol [in the Isfahan copy: "the greatest" instead of "the largest"] remained; he hung the axe around its neck and went out. This is His saying: ﴿So he made them into fragments﴾.

Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash and al-Kisa'i read it with a kasra on the jim, meaning fragments and pieces, plural of judhadh, which is dry crumbled stalk, like khafif and khiffaf, karim and kiram. The rest read it with a damma, meaning debris and fine fragments. ﴿Except a great one among them﴾, meaning the largest of the gods, for he did not break it, and placed the axe on its neck. ﴿So that they might return to it﴾, so that they would reflect and know its weakness and powerlessness. It was also said: ﴿So that they might return to it﴾ and ask it.

When the people came back from their festival to the house of their gods and saw their idols, they said: ﴿Who has done this to our gods? Indeed, he is among the wrongdoers.﴾ They said, meaning those who had heard Abraham say: ﴿By Allah, I will surely plot against your idols﴾ ... ﴿We heard a youth mention them﴾, disparaging them, reviling them, and mocking them, ﴿called Abraham﴾: he is the one who did this. The news reached Nimrod the tyrant and the nobles of his people, and they said: ﴿Bring him before the eyes of the people﴾, meaning, in the sight of the people [in the Isfahan copy: It was said: it means "before the heads of the people"; and it was said it means "in their view"; they intended by this "in plain view", and the one who did it is for the people, as the Arabs say when a matter is made public and widespread: "That happened before the eyes of the people"], ﴿so that they may bear witness against him that he is the one who did that﴾, and they disliked taking him without evidence. This was said by Qatadah and al-Suddi.

Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: ﴿So that they may witness what is done to him and what punishment he receives﴾, that is, that they may be present. When they brought him, they said: ﴿Did you do this to our gods, O Abraham?﴾ Abraham said: ﴿Rather, it was done by this, their chief; so ask them, if they can speak.﴾ This is a rebuke over their worship of these small ones alongside this great one, which is greater than them, so he broke them. This was said by Ibn Ishaq, and Abraham intended by it to establish proof against them, which is the meaning of His saying: ﴿So ask them, if they can speak﴾, until they inform you who did this to them.

It is narrated from al-Kisa'i that he would pause at His saying "Rather, it was done by" and say: its meaning is "it was done by the one who did it", then start again with "this, their chief".

Al-Qutaybi said: Abraham made speech a condition for the act, saying: ﴿It was done by this, their chief; so ask them if they can speak﴾, and the meaning is: if they are able to act. He showed them their inability to speak and act. Implicit in this is: "I did that." What the reports agree upon regarding this verse is the saying of Ibn Ishaq, which indicates it.

The saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Abraham did not lie except three lies, all of them concerning Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: his saying ﴿I am sick﴾ [al-Saffat: 89], his saying ﴿Rather, it was done by this, their chief﴾, and his saying to Sarah: 'She is my sister.'"

It is not impossible that Allah, glorified is He, permitted His messenger and close friend to do this, in order to shame his people, rebuke them, argue against them, and make known to them the place of their error, just as He permitted it for Joseph when he commanded his crier who said to his brothers: ﴿O caravan, indeed you are thieves﴾ [Yusuf: 70], though they had not stolen anything.

﴿So they returned to themselves﴾: meaning they reflected in their hearts and returned to their minds, and they said: ﴿You have indeed wronged yourselves﴾ by asking him, since this is your gods, and what was done to them is evident, so ask them. It was also said: ﴿You are indeed the wrongdoers﴾ by your worship of small idols alongside this great one.

Then they were overturned upon their heads, bewildered and perplexed, and they knew that the idols do not speak nor strike. They said: ﴿You know well that these do not speak.﴾ When the proof turned against them, Abraham said to them: ﴿Do you worship besides Allah what neither benefits you at all nor harms you? Uff to you and to what you worship besides Allah! Will you not reason?﴾ When the proof was binding upon them and they were unable to answer, they said: ﴿Burn him and support your gods, if you are going to act.﴾

Ibn Umar [in the Isfahan copy: Abu Umar] said: The one who advised them to burn Abraham was a man from the Kurds. Shu'ayb al-Jubba'i said: his name was Haizan, and Allah caused the earth to swallow him, and he will keep sinking into it until the Day of Resurrection. They said: When Nimrod gathered his people to burn Abraham, they imprisoned him in a house and built a structure like an enclosure. This is His saying: ﴿They said: Build for him a structure and throw him into the blazing fire﴾ [al-Saffat: 97]. Then they gathered for him hard firewood of various kinds, so much that a woman who fell ill would say: "If he restores my health, I will surely gather firewood for Abraham." A woman would vow, in some matter she sought and loved to attain, that if it came to pass she would gather firewood for the fire of Abraham, by which he would be burned, as an act of devotion in her religion.

Ibn Ishaq said: They gathered firewood for a month. They said: Until, when they had gathered as much as they wanted, they lit fire at every side of the wood, and the fire blazed and grew so intense that a bird passing by would be burned from its intense heat. Then they went to Abraham, lifted him to the top of the structure, and bound him. Then they made a catapult and placed him in it, shackled and chained. The heavens and the earth, and whoever is in them of the angels and all creation except the two jinn and humans, cried out with one cry: "O our Lord, Abraham is not on Your earth anyone who worships You besides him, and he is to be burned for You. So permit us to help him." Allah, glorified and exalted, said to them: "If he calls upon any of you for help, let him help him, for I have permitted him in that. If he calls upon none but Me, then I know him best, and I am his protector. So leave him to Me." When they wanted to throw him into the fire, the keeper of the waters came to him and said: "If you wish, I will extinguish the fire, for the treasures of the rains are in my hand." The keeper of the winds came to him and said: "If you wish, I will scatter the fire into the air." Abraham said: "I have no need of you." Then he raised his head to the sky and said: "O Allah, You are the One in the heavens, and I am the one on the earth; there is no one on the earth who worships You besides me. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs."

Al-Mu'tamir narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from Arqam, that Abraham said when they bound him to throw him into the fire: "There is no god but You, glory be to You, Lord of the worlds; to You is praise and to You is dominion; You have no partner." He said: Then they threw him from a great distance into the fire by catapult, and Gabriel met him and said: "O Abraham, do you have any need?" He said: "As for you, no." Gabriel said: "Then ask your Lord." Abraham said: "My knowledge of my condition is sufficient for my request." Then Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿O fire, be cool and safe for Abraham.﴾ Al-Suddi said: Gabriel was the one who called to it.

Ibn Abbas said: If its coolness had not been followed by "safety," Abraham would have died from its cold. Thus no fire remained that day on earth but was extinguished, thinking that it was meant by this.

Al-Suddi said: The angels took Abraham by his armpits and seated him on the ground, and there was a spring of sweet water, a red flower, and narcissus.

Ka'b said: The fire burned nothing of Abraham except his bonds. They said: Abraham remained in that place for seven days.

Al-Minhal ibn Amr said: Abraham, the friend of Allah, said: "I never had days more pleasant than the days I spent in the fire."

Ibn Yasar said: Allah, whose name is majestic, sent the angel of shade in the form of Abraham, and he sat in the fire beside Abraham, keeping him company. They said: Allah sent him a shirt of silk from Paradise, and Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to him and said: "O Abraham, your Lord says: Did you not know that fire does not harm My beloved?" Then Nimrod looked out from a palace he had, and overlooked Abraham, and had no doubt of his death. He saw Abraham sitting in a garden, and saw the angel sitting beside him, and around him was fire burning what they had gathered of firewood. Nimrod called out: "O Abraham, is your God great, whose power has reached the point that He has prevented between you and what I see, so it did not harm you? O Abraham, can you come out of it?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Do you fear that if you remain in it, it will harm you?" He said: "No." He said: "Then get up and come out of it." Abraham got up walking in it until he came out of it. When he came out to him, he said: "O Abraham, who is the man I saw with you, sitting beside you, resembling your form?" He said: "That is the angel of shade, whom my Lord sent to keep me company in it." Nimrod said: "O Abraham, I will offer a sacrifice to your God, because of what I saw of His power and might in what He did for you, when you refused anything but His worship and His unity. I will slaughter for Him four thousand cows." Abraham said to him: "Then Allah will not accept from you while you remain on this religion of yours, until you leave it for my religion." He said: "O Abraham, I cannot leave my kingship, but I will slaughter them for Him." So Nimrod slaughtered them for Him. Then he withheld from Abraham, and Allah, glorified is He, protected him from him.

Abu Hurayrah said: The best thing Abraham said, when the covering was lifted from him while he was in the fire and his forehead was sweating, was: Nimrod said at that: "Excellent is your Lord, O Abraham." Ka'b, Qatadah and al-Zuhri said: No one among the people of the earth benefited that day from the fire, and the fire burned nothing that day except Abraham's bonds, and no creature came that day but it extinguished the fire from him, except the gecko (al-wazagh). For this reason the Prophet ﷺ commanded its killing and named it "fuwaysiq" (the mischievous little one).

Shu'ayb al-Jubba'i said: Abraham (peace be upon him) was thrown into the fire when he was sixteen years old; Isaac was sacrificed when he was seven years old; Sarah bore him when she was ninety years old; and his place of sacrifice was from the House of Iliya, two miles away. When Sarah learned what he intended with Isaac, she wailed that day and died on the third day.

Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿And they intended a scheme against him, but We made them the greatest losers.﴾ ﴿And We delivered him and Lot to the land which We had blessed for the worlds﴾, meaning from Nimrod and his people, from the land of Iraq, to the land, meaning Syria.

Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: He called it blessed because there is no sweet water but that its source springs from under the rock that is in Bayt al-Maqdis.

Qatadah said: It was said: Syria is the outskirts of the abode of emigration; what is lacking from the land is added to Syria, and what is lacking from Syria is added to Palestine. It was said: It is the land of the gathering and the resurrection, the place where people assemble, where Jesus son of Mary will descend, and where Allah will destroy the Dajjal.

Abu Qilabah narrated that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "I saw in a dream as if the angels carried the pillar of the Book and placed it in Syria. I interpreted that when trials occur, faith is in Syria."

It has been mentioned to us that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said to Ka'b: "Would you not move to Medina, for it is the place of emigration of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the site of his grave?" Ka'b said to him: "O Commander of the Faithful, I find in the revealed Book of Allah that Syria is the treasure of Allah from His earth, and there is His treasure from His servants."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said: Some men of his people responded to Abraham when they saw what Allah, glorified is He, had done to him, making the fire ﴿cool and safe﴾, in fear of Nimrod and his chiefs. ﴿Lot believed in him﴾; he was his nephew, Lot son of Haran son of Terah. Haran was the brother of Abraham, and he had a third brother called Bahur son of Terah. Haran was the father of Lot; Nahur was the father of Tabwil; Tabwil was the father of Lan; and Ratqa, daughter of Tabwil, was the wife of Isaac son of Abraham, mother of Jacob; Liya and Zajil, the two daughters of Layan, were the wives of Jacob. Sarah also believed in him; she was the daughter of his paternal uncle, Sarah daughter of Haran the elder, paternal uncle of Abraham, peace be upon him.

Al-Suddi said: Sarah was the daughter of the king of Harran. Abraham and Lot set out toward Syria, and Abraham met Sarah, who was the daughter of the king of Harran, and she had criticized her people for their religion; Abraham married her on condition that he would change her.

Ibn Ishaq said: Abraham left Kuthā in the land of Iraq as an emigrant to his Lord, and Lot and Sarah went out with him, as Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿Lot believed in him, and [Abraham] said: Indeed I am emigrating to my Lord﴾. He went out seeking refuge for his religion and security for the worship of Allah, until he settled in Harran and remained there as long as Allah willed. Then he left it as an emigrant until he came to Egypt, then left Egypt for Syria and settled in al-Sab' in the land of Palestine, which is the desert of Syria. Lot settled at al-Mu'tafikah, which is one day and night's journey or a little more from al-Sab', and Allah, glorified is He, sent him as a prophet. This is His saying: ﴿And We delivered him and Lot to the land which We had blessed for the worlds﴾, meaning Syria. Its blessing is that most of the prophets were sent from it; it is a fertile land abounding in trees, rivers, and fruits, where the life of the poor and the rich is pleasant.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿to the land which We had blessed for the worlds﴾: he said: it means Mecca and the settling of Ishmael. Do you not see that He says: ﴿Indeed, the first House established for mankind is that at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for the worlds﴾ [Al 'Imran: 96]? But the first opinion is more correct.

﴿And We gave him Isaac and Jacob as an additional gift (nafilah)﴾, meaning a gift; from Mujahid. Al-Hasan and al-Dahhak said: an extra favor. Ibn Abbas, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Ibn Zayd and Qatadah said: He asked for one, saying: ﴿My Lord, grant me of the righteous﴾, so Allah gave him Isaac as a son, and increased him with Jacob, a grandson, and that is the nafilah. Mujahid and Ata' said: the meaning of nafilah is gift, and both were from the bounty of Allah, glorified is He, Who gave them to him.

﴿And We made all of them righteous﴾, meaning Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, peace be upon them.

And We had certainly given Abraham his right judgment (rushdahu), meaning his tawfiq (divine enabling). Al-Qurazi said: his righteousness, from before (min qablu), meaning before Moses and Aaron.

The exegetes said: That is, We guided him while he was young, as He said regarding Yahya: ﴿And We gave him judgment while still a boy﴾ [Maryam: 12].

And We had knowledge of him, that he was one fit for guidance and prophethood.

When he said to his father and his people: ﴿What are these statues and images to which you are devoted?﴾ That is, the idols that you are devoted to, persisting in their worship.

They said: ﴿We found our fathers worshipping them﴾, so we follow them.

He said: ﴿Indeed you and your fathers have been in clear error﴾ by your worship of them.

They said: ﴿Have you brought us the truth, or are you among the jesters?﴾ meaning: Are you serious in what you say, or are you joking?

He said: ﴿Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who created them (fatarahunna)﴾, meaning, who created them; ﴿and I am among the witnesses to that. And by Allah, I will surely plot against your idols after you have turned away, retreating﴾, meaning, I will surely scheme against them.

Mujahid and Qatadah said: Abraham said this secretly among his people, and only one man among them heard it, and he is the one who disclosed it, saying: ﴿We heard a youth mention them, called Abraham﴾.

Al-Suddi said: They had a yearly assembly and festival. Whenever they returned from their festival, they would enter upon the idols and prostrate to them, then return to their homes. When that festival came, Abraham's father said to him: "O Abraham, if you came out with us to our festival, our religion would please you." So Abraham went out with them. When he was on part of the road, he threw himself down and said: ﴿Indeed, I am sick﴾, meaning: "I am complaining of my leg." So they left him, and he lay there prostrate. When they had gone, he called out after the last of them, when only a few people remained: ﴿By Allah, I will surely plot against your idols after you have turned away, retreating﴾, and they heard it from him. Then Abraham returned to the gods, and found them in a great hall, facing the door of the hall was a great idol, and beside it smaller ones, one beside another, each idol next to it smaller than it, down to the door of the hall. They had placed food before the idols and said: "When we return, the gods will have blessed our food, and we will eat it." When Abraham looked at them and at the food before them, he said to them in mockery: ﴿Will you not eat?﴾ When none of them answered, he said: ﴿What is wrong with you that you do not speak?﴾ Then he turned upon them, striking them with his right hand, and began to break them with an axe in his hand, until only the largest idol [in the Isfahan copy: "the greatest" instead of "the largest"] remained; he hung the axe around its neck and went out. This is His saying: ﴿So he made them into fragments﴾.

Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash and al-Kisa'i read it with a kasra on the jim, meaning fragments and pieces, plural of judhadh, which is dry crumbled stalk, like khafif and khiffaf, karim and kiram. The rest read it with a damma, meaning debris and fine fragments. ﴿Except a great one among them﴾, meaning the largest of the gods, for he did not break it, and placed the axe on its neck. ﴿So that they might return to it﴾, so that they would reflect and know its weakness and powerlessness. It was also said: ﴿So that they might return to it﴾ and ask it.

When the people came back from their festival to the house of their gods and saw their idols, they said: ﴿Who has done this to our gods? Indeed, he is among the wrongdoers.﴾ They said, meaning those who had heard Abraham say: ﴿By Allah, I will surely plot against your idols﴾ ... ﴿We heard a youth mention them﴾, disparaging them, reviling them, and mocking them, ﴿called Abraham﴾: he is the one who did this. The news reached Nimrod the tyrant and the nobles of his people, and they said: ﴿Bring him before the eyes of the people﴾, meaning, in the sight of the people [in the Isfahan copy: It was said: it means "before the heads of the people"; and it was said it means "in their view"; they intended by this "in plain view", and the one who did it is for the people, as the Arabs say when a matter is made public and widespread: "That happened before the eyes of the people"], ﴿so that they may bear witness against him that he is the one who did that﴾, and they disliked taking him without evidence. This was said by Qatadah and al-Suddi.

Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: ﴿So that they may witness what is done to him and what punishment he receives﴾, that is, that they may be present. When they brought him, they said: ﴿Did you do this to our gods, O Abraham?﴾ Abraham said: ﴿Rather, it was done by this, their chief; so ask them, if they can speak.﴾ This is a rebuke over their worship of these small ones alongside this great one, which is greater than them, so he broke them. This was said by Ibn Ishaq, and Abraham intended by it to establish proof against them, which is the meaning of His saying: ﴿So ask them, if they can speak﴾, until they inform you who did this to them.

It is narrated from al-Kisa'i that he would pause at His saying "Rather, it was done by" and say: its meaning is "it was done by the one who did it", then start again with "this, their chief".

Al-Qutaybi said: Abraham made speech a condition for the act, saying: ﴿It was done by this, their chief; so ask them if they can speak﴾, and the meaning is: if they are able to act. He showed them their inability to speak and act. Implicit in this is: "I did that." What the reports agree upon regarding this verse is the saying of Ibn Ishaq, which indicates it.

The saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Abraham did not lie except three lies, all of them concerning Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: his saying ﴿I am sick﴾ [al-Saffat: 89], his saying ﴿Rather, it was done by this, their chief﴾, and his saying to Sarah: 'She is my sister.'"

It is not impossible that Allah, glorified is He, permitted His messenger and close friend to do this, in order to shame his people, rebuke them, argue against them, and make known to them the place of their error, just as He permitted it for Joseph when he commanded his crier who said to his brothers: ﴿O caravan, indeed you are thieves﴾ [Yusuf: 70], though they had not stolen anything.

﴿So they returned to themselves﴾: meaning they reflected in their hearts and returned to their minds, and they said: ﴿You have indeed wronged yourselves﴾ by asking him, since this is your gods, and what was done to them is evident, so ask them. It was also said: ﴿You are indeed the wrongdoers﴾ by your worship of small idols alongside this great one.

Then they were overturned upon their heads, bewildered and perplexed, and they knew that the idols do not speak nor strike. They said: ﴿You know well that these do not speak.﴾ When the proof turned against them, Abraham said to them: ﴿Do you worship besides Allah what neither benefits you at all nor harms you? Uff to you and to what you worship besides Allah! Will you not reason?﴾ When the proof was binding upon them and they were unable to answer, they said: ﴿Burn him and support your gods, if you are going to act.﴾

Ibn Umar [in the Isfahan copy: Abu Umar] said: The one who advised them to burn Abraham was a man from the Kurds. Shu'ayb al-Jubba'i said: his name was Haizan, and Allah caused the earth to swallow him, and he will keep sinking into it until the Day of Resurrection. They said: When Nimrod gathered his people to burn Abraham, they imprisoned him in a house and built a structure like an enclosure. This is His saying: ﴿They said: Build for him a structure and throw him into the blazing fire﴾ [al-Saffat: 97]. Then they gathered for him hard firewood of various kinds, so much that a woman who fell ill would say: "If he restores my health, I will surely gather firewood for Abraham." A woman would vow, in some matter she sought and loved to attain, that if it came to pass she would gather firewood for the fire of Abraham, by which he would be burned, as an act of devotion in her religion.

Ibn Ishaq said: They gathered firewood for a month. They said: Until, when they had gathered as much as they wanted, they lit fire at every side of the wood, and the fire blazed and grew so intense that a bird passing by would be burned from its intense heat. Then they went to Abraham, lifted him to the top of the structure, and bound him. Then they made a catapult and placed him in it, shackled and chained. The heavens and the earth, and whoever is in them of the angels and all creation except the two jinn and humans, cried out with one cry: "O our Lord, Abraham is not on Your earth anyone who worships You besides him, and he is to be burned for You. So permit us to help him." Allah, glorified and exalted, said to them: "If he calls upon any of you for help, let him help him, for I have permitted him in that. If he calls upon none but Me, then I know him best, and I am his protector. So leave him to Me." When they wanted to throw him into the fire, the keeper of the waters came to him and said: "If you wish, I will extinguish the fire, for the treasures of the rains are in my hand." The keeper of the winds came to him and said: "If you wish, I will scatter the fire into the air." Abraham said: "I have no need of you." Then he raised his head to the sky and said: "O Allah, You are the One in the heavens, and I am the one on the earth; there is no one on the earth who worships You besides me. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs."

Al-Mu'tamir narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from Arqam, that Abraham said when they bound him to throw him into the fire: "There is no god but You, glory be to You, Lord of the worlds; to You is praise and to You is dominion; You have no partner." He said: Then they threw him from a great distance into the fire by catapult, and Gabriel met him and said: "O Abraham, do you have any need?" He said: "As for you, no." Gabriel said: "Then ask your Lord." Abraham said: "My knowledge of my condition is sufficient for my request." Then Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿O fire, be cool and safe for Abraham.﴾ Al-Suddi said: Gabriel was the one who called to it.

Ibn Abbas said: If its coolness had not been followed by "safety," Abraham would have died from its cold. Thus no fire remained that day on earth but was extinguished, thinking that it was meant by this.

Al-Suddi said: The angels took Abraham by his armpits and seated him on the ground, and there was a spring of sweet water, a red flower, and narcissus.

Ka'b said: The fire burned nothing of Abraham except his bonds. They said: Abraham remained in that place for seven days.

Al-Minhal ibn Amr said: Abraham, the friend of Allah, said: "I never had days more pleasant than the days I spent in the fire."

Ibn Yasar said: Allah, whose name is majestic, sent the angel of shade in the form of Abraham, and he sat in the fire beside Abraham, keeping him company. They said: Allah sent him a shirt of silk from Paradise, and Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to him and said: "O Abraham, your Lord says: Did you not know that fire does not harm My beloved?" Then Nimrod looked out from a palace he had, and overlooked Abraham, and had no doubt of his death. He saw Abraham sitting in a garden, and saw the angel sitting beside him, and around him was fire burning what they had gathered of firewood. Nimrod called out: "O Abraham, is your God great, whose power has reached the point that He has prevented between you and what I see, so it did not harm you? O Abraham, can you come out of it?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Do you fear that if you remain in it, it will harm you?" He said: "No." He said: "Then get up and come out of it." Abraham got up walking in it until he came out of it. When he came out to him, he said: "O Abraham, who is the man I saw with you, sitting beside you, resembling your form?" He said: "That is the angel of shade, whom my Lord sent to keep me company in it." Nimrod said: "O Abraham, I will offer a sacrifice to your God, because of what I saw of His power and might in what He did for you, when you refused anything but His worship and His unity. I will slaughter for Him four thousand cows." Abraham said to him: "Then Allah will not accept from you while you remain on this religion of yours, until you leave it for my religion." He said: "O Abraham, I cannot leave my kingship, but I will slaughter them for Him." So Nimrod slaughtered them for Him. Then he withheld from Abraham, and Allah, glorified is He, protected him from him.

Abu Hurayrah said: The best thing Abraham said, when the covering was lifted from him while he was in the fire and his forehead was sweating, was: Nimrod said at that: "Excellent is your Lord, O Abraham." Ka'b, Qatadah and al-Zuhri said: No one among the people of the earth benefited that day from the fire, and the fire burned nothing that day except Abraham's bonds, and no creature came that day but it extinguished the fire from him, except the gecko (al-wazagh). For this reason the Prophet ﷺ commanded its killing and named it "fuwaysiq" (the mischievous little one).

Shu'ayb al-Jubba'i said: Abraham (peace be upon him) was thrown into the fire when he was sixteen years old; Isaac was sacrificed when he was seven years old; Sarah bore him when she was ninety years old; and his place of sacrifice was from the House of Iliya, two miles away. When Sarah learned what he intended with Isaac, she wailed that day and died on the third day.

Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿And they intended a scheme against him, but We made them the greatest losers.﴾ ﴿And We delivered him and Lot to the land which We had blessed for the worlds﴾, meaning from Nimrod and his people, from the land of Iraq, to the land, meaning Syria.

Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: He called it blessed because there is no sweet water but that its source springs from under the rock that is in Bayt al-Maqdis.

Qatadah said: It was said: Syria is the outskirts of the abode of emigration; what is lacking from the land is added to Syria, and what is lacking from Syria is added to Palestine. It was said: It is the land of the gathering and the resurrection, the place where people assemble, where Jesus son of Mary will descend, and where Allah will destroy the Dajjal.

Abu Qilabah narrated that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "I saw in a dream as if the angels carried the pillar of the Book and placed it in Syria. I interpreted that when trials occur, faith is in Syria."

It has been mentioned to us that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said to Ka'b: "Would you not move to Medina, for it is the place of emigration of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the site of his grave?" Ka'b said to him: "O Commander of the Faithful, I find in the revealed Book of Allah that Syria is the treasure of Allah from His earth, and there is His treasure from His servants."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said: Some men of his people responded to Abraham when they saw what Allah, glorified is He, had done to him, making the fire ﴿cool and safe﴾, in fear of Nimrod and his chiefs. ﴿Lot believed in him﴾; he was his nephew, Lot son of Haran son of Terah. Haran was the brother of Abraham, and he had a third brother called Bahur son of Terah. Haran was the father of Lot; Nahur was the father of Tabwil; Tabwil was the father of Lan; and Ratqa, daughter of Tabwil, was the wife of Isaac son of Abraham, mother of Jacob; Liya and Zajil, the two daughters of Layan, were the wives of Jacob. Sarah also believed in him; she was the daughter of his paternal uncle, Sarah daughter of Haran the elder, paternal uncle of Abraham, peace be upon him.

Al-Suddi said: Sarah was the daughter of the king of Harran. Abraham and Lot set out toward Syria, and Abraham met Sarah, who was the daughter of the king of Harran, and she had criticized her people for their religion; Abraham married her on condition that he would change her.

Ibn Ishaq said: Abraham left Kuthā in the land of Iraq as an emigrant to his Lord, and Lot and Sarah went out with him, as Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿Lot believed in him, and [Abraham] said: Indeed I am emigrating to my Lord﴾. He went out seeking refuge for his religion and security for the worship of Allah, until he settled in Harran and remained there as long as Allah willed. Then he left it as an emigrant until he came to Egypt, then left Egypt for Syria and settled in al-Sab' in the land of Palestine, which is the desert of Syria. Lot settled at al-Mu'tafikah, which is one day and night's journey or a little more from al-Sab', and Allah, glorified is He, sent him as a prophet. This is His saying: ﴿And We delivered him and Lot to the land which We had blessed for the worlds﴾, meaning Syria. Its blessing is that most of the prophets were sent from it; it is a fertile land abounding in trees, rivers, and fruits, where the life of the poor and the rich is pleasant.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿to the land which We had blessed for the worlds﴾: he said: it means Mecca and the settling of Ishmael. Do you not see that He says: ﴿Indeed, the first House established for mankind is that at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for the worlds﴾ [Al 'Imran: 96]? But the first opinion is more correct.

﴿And We gave him Isaac and Jacob as an additional gift (nafilah)﴾, meaning a gift; from Mujahid. Al-Hasan and al-Dahhak said: an extra favor. Ibn Abbas, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Ibn Zayd and Qatadah said: He asked for one, saying: ﴿My Lord, grant me of the righteous﴾, so Allah gave him Isaac as a son, and increased him with Jacob, a grandson, and that is the nafilah. Mujahid and Ata' said: the meaning of nafilah is gift, and both were from the bounty of Allah, glorified is He, Who gave them to him.

﴿And We made all of them righteous﴾, meaning Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, peace be upon them.

And We had certainly given Abraham his right judgment (rushdahu), meaning his tawfiq (divine enabling). Al-Qurazi said: his righteousness, from before (min qablu), meaning before Moses and Aaron.

The exegetes said: That is, We guided him while he was young, as He said regarding Yahya: ﴿And We gave him judgment while still a boy﴾ [Maryam: 12].

And We had knowledge of him, that he was one fit for guidance and prophethood.

When he said to his father and his people: ﴿What are these statues and images to which you are devoted?﴾ That is, the idols that you are devoted to, persisting in their worship.

They said: ﴿We found our fathers worshipping them﴾, so we follow them.

He said: ﴿Indeed you and your fathers have been in clear error﴾ by your worship of them.

They said: ﴿Have you brought us the truth, or are you among the jesters?﴾ meaning: Are you serious in what you say, or are you joking?

He said: ﴿Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who created them (fatarahunna)﴾, meaning, who created them; ﴿and I am among the witnesses to that. And by Allah, I will surely plot against your idols after you have turned away, retreating﴾, meaning, I will surely scheme against them.

Mujahid and Qatadah said: Abraham said this secretly among his people, and only one man among them heard it, and he is the one who disclosed it, saying: ﴿We heard a youth mention them, called Abraham﴾.

Al-Suddi said: They had a yearly assembly and festival. Whenever they returned from their festival, they would enter upon the idols and prostrate to them, then return to their homes. When that festival came, Abraham's father said to him: "O Abraham, if you came out with us to our festival, our religion would please you." So Abraham went out with them. When he was on part of the road, he threw himself down and said: ﴿Indeed, I am sick﴾, meaning: "I am complaining of my leg." So they left him, and he lay there prostrate. When they had gone, he called out after the last of them, when only a few people remained: ﴿By Allah, I will surely plot against your idols after you have turned away, retreating﴾, and they heard it from him. Then Abraham returned to the gods, and found them in a great hall, facing the door of the hall was a great idol, and beside it smaller ones, one beside another, each idol next to it smaller than it, down to the door of the hall. They had placed food before the idols and said: "When we return, the gods will have blessed our food, and we will eat it." When Abraham looked at them and at the food before them, he said to them in mockery: ﴿Will you not eat?﴾ When none of them answered, he said: ﴿What is wrong with you that you do not speak?﴾ Then he turned upon them, striking them with his right hand, and began to break them with an axe in his hand, until only the largest idol [in the Isfahan copy: "the greatest" instead of "the largest"] remained; he hung the axe around its neck and went out. This is His saying: ﴿So he made them into fragments﴾.

Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash and al-Kisa'i read it with a kasra on the jim, meaning fragments and pieces, plural of judhadh, which is dry crumbled stalk, like khafif and khiffaf, karim and kiram. The rest read it with a damma, meaning debris and fine fragments. ﴿Except a great one among them﴾, meaning the largest of the gods, for he did not break it, and placed the axe on its neck. ﴿So that they might return to it﴾, so that they would reflect and know its weakness and powerlessness. It was also said: ﴿So that they might return to it﴾ and ask it.

When the people came back from their festival to the house of their gods and saw their idols, they said: ﴿Who has done this to our gods? Indeed, he is among the wrongdoers.﴾ They said, meaning those who had heard Abraham say: ﴿By Allah, I will surely plot against your idols﴾ ... ﴿We heard a youth mention them﴾, disparaging them, reviling them, and mocking them, ﴿called Abraham﴾: he is the one who did this. The news reached Nimrod the tyrant and the nobles of his people, and they said: ﴿Bring him before the eyes of the people﴾, meaning, in the sight of the people [in the Isfahan copy: It was said: it means "before the heads of the people"; and it was said it means "in their view"; they intended by this "in plain view", and the one who did it is for the people, as the Arabs say when a matter is made public and widespread: "That happened before the eyes of the people"], ﴿so that they may bear witness against him that he is the one who did that﴾, and they disliked taking him without evidence. This was said by Qatadah and al-Suddi.

Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: ﴿So that they may witness what is done to him and what punishment he receives﴾, that is, that they may be present. When they brought him, they said: ﴿Did you do this to our gods, O Abraham?﴾ Abraham said: ﴿Rather, it was done by this, their chief; so ask them, if they can speak.﴾ This is a rebuke over their worship of these small ones alongside this great one, which is greater than them, so he broke them. This was said by Ibn Ishaq, and Abraham intended by it to establish proof against them, which is the meaning of His saying: ﴿So ask them, if they can speak﴾, until they inform you who did this to them.

It is narrated from al-Kisa'i that he would pause at His saying "Rather, it was done by" and say: its meaning is "it was done by the one who did it", then start again with "this, their chief".

Al-Qutaybi said: Abraham made speech a condition for the act, saying: ﴿It was done by this, their chief; so ask them if they can speak﴾, and the meaning is: if they are able to act. He showed them their inability to speak and act. Implicit in this is: "I did that." What the reports agree upon regarding this verse is the saying of Ibn Ishaq, which indicates it.

The saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Abraham did not lie except three lies, all of them concerning Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: his saying ﴿I am sick﴾ [al-Saffat: 89], his saying ﴿Rather, it was done by this, their chief﴾, and his saying to Sarah: 'She is my sister.'"

It is not impossible that Allah, glorified is He, permitted His messenger and close friend to do this, in order to shame his people, rebuke them, argue against them, and make known to them the place of their error, just as He permitted it for Joseph when he commanded his crier who said to his brothers: ﴿O caravan, indeed you are thieves﴾ [Yusuf: 70], though they had not stolen anything.

﴿So they returned to themselves﴾: meaning they reflected in their hearts and returned to their minds, and they said: ﴿You have indeed wronged yourselves﴾ by asking him, since this is your gods, and what was done to them is evident, so ask them. It was also said: ﴿You are indeed the wrongdoers﴾ by your worship of small idols alongside this great one.

Then they were overturned upon their heads, bewildered and perplexed, and they knew that the idols do not speak nor strike. They said: ﴿You know well that these do not speak.﴾ When the proof turned against them, Abraham said to them: ﴿Do you worship besides Allah what neither benefits you at all nor harms you? Uff to you and to what you worship besides Allah! Will you not reason?﴾ When the proof was binding upon them and they were unable to answer, they said: ﴿Burn him and support your gods, if you are going to act.﴾

Ibn Umar [in the Isfahan copy: Abu Umar] said: The one who advised them to burn Abraham was a man from the Kurds. Shu'ayb al-Jubba'i said: his name was Haizan, and Allah caused the earth to swallow him, and he will keep sinking into it until the Day of Resurrection. They said: When Nimrod gathered his people to burn Abraham, they imprisoned him in a house and built a structure like an enclosure. This is His saying: ﴿They said: Build for him a structure and throw him into the blazing fire﴾ [al-Saffat: 97]. Then they gathered for him hard firewood of various kinds, so much that a woman who fell ill would say: "If he restores my health, I will surely gather firewood for Abraham." A woman would vow, in some matter she sought and loved to attain, that if it came to pass she would gather firewood for the fire of Abraham, by which he would be burned, as an act of devotion in her religion.

Ibn Ishaq said: They gathered firewood for a month. They said: Until, when they had gathered as much as they wanted, they lit fire at every side of the wood, and the fire blazed and grew so intense that a bird passing by would be burned from its intense heat. Then they went to Abraham, lifted him to the top of the structure, and bound him. Then they made a catapult and placed him in it, shackled and chained. The heavens and the earth, and whoever is in them of the angels and all creation except the two jinn and humans, cried out with one cry: "O our Lord, Abraham is not on Your earth anyone who worships You besides him, and he is to be burned for You. So permit us to help him." Allah, glorified and exalted, said to them: "If he calls upon any of you for help, let him help him, for I have permitted him in that. If he calls upon none but Me, then I know him best, and I am his protector. So leave him to Me." When they wanted to throw him into the fire, the keeper of the waters came to him and said: "If you wish, I will extinguish the fire, for the treasures of the rains are in my hand." The keeper of the winds came to him and said: "If you wish, I will scatter the fire into the air." Abraham said: "I have no need of you." Then he raised his head to the sky and said: "O Allah, You are the One in the heavens, and I am the one on the earth; there is no one on the earth who worships You besides me. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs."

Al-Mu'tamir narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from Arqam, that Abraham said when they bound him to throw him into the fire: "There is no god but You, glory be to You, Lord of the worlds; to You is praise and to You is dominion; You have no partner." He said: Then they threw him from a great distance into the fire by catapult, and Gabriel met him and said: "O Abraham, do you have any need?" He said: "As for you, no." Gabriel said: "Then ask your Lord." Abraham said: "My knowledge of my condition is sufficient for my request." Then Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿O fire, be cool and safe for Abraham.﴾ Al-Suddi said: Gabriel was the one who called to it.

Ibn Abbas said: If its coolness had not been followed by "safety," Abraham would have died from its cold. Thus no fire remained that day on earth but was extinguished, thinking that it was meant by this.

Al-Suddi said: The angels took Abraham by his armpits and seated him on the ground, and there was a spring of sweet water, a red flower, and narcissus.

Ka'b said: The fire burned nothing of Abraham except his bonds. They said: Abraham remained in that place for seven days.

Al-Minhal ibn Amr said: Abraham, the friend of Allah, said: "I never had days more pleasant than the days I spent in the fire."

Ibn Yasar said: Allah, whose name is majestic, sent the angel of shade in the form of Abraham, and he sat in the fire beside Abraham, keeping him company. They said: Allah sent him a shirt of silk from Paradise, and Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to him and said: "O Abraham, your Lord says: Did you not know that fire does not harm My beloved?" Then Nimrod looked out from a palace he had, and overlooked Abraham, and had no doubt of his death. He saw Abraham sitting in a garden, and saw the angel sitting beside him, and around him was fire burning what they had gathered of firewood. Nimrod called out: "O Abraham, is your God great, whose power has reached the point that He has prevented between you and what I see, so it did not harm you? O Abraham, can you come out of it?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Do you fear that if you remain in it, it will harm you?" He said: "No." He said: "Then get up and come out of it." Abraham got up walking in it until he came out of it. When he came out to him, he said: "O Abraham, who is the man I saw with you, sitting beside you, resembling your form?" He said: "That is the angel of shade, whom my Lord sent to keep me company in it." Nimrod said: "O Abraham, I will offer a sacrifice to your God, because of what I saw of His power and might in what He did for you, when you refused anything but His worship and His unity. I will slaughter for Him four thousand cows." Abraham said to him: "Then Allah will not accept from you while you remain on this religion of yours, until you leave it for my religion." He said: "O Abraham, I cannot leave my kingship, but I will slaughter them for Him." So Nimrod slaughtered them for Him. Then he withheld from Abraham, and Allah, glorified is He, protected him from him.

Abu Hurayrah said: The best thing Abraham said, when the covering was lifted from him while he was in the fire and his forehead was sweating, was: Nimrod said at that: "Excellent is your Lord, O Abraham." Ka'b, Qatadah and al-Zuhri said: No one among the people of the earth benefited that day from the fire, and the fire burned nothing that day except Abraham's bonds, and no creature came that day but it extinguished the fire from him, except the gecko (al-wazagh). For this reason the Prophet ﷺ commanded its killing and named it "fuwaysiq" (the mischievous little one).

Shu'ayb al-Jubba'i said: Abraham (peace be upon him) was thrown into the fire when he was sixteen years old; Isaac was sacrificed when he was seven years old; Sarah bore him when she was ninety years old; and his place of sacrifice was from the House of Iliya, two miles away. When Sarah learned what he intended with Isaac, she wailed that day and died on the third day.

Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿And they intended a scheme against him, but We made them the greatest losers.﴾ ﴿And We delivered him and Lot to the land which We had blessed for the worlds﴾, meaning from Nimrod and his people, from the land of Iraq, to the land, meaning Syria.

Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: He called it blessed because there is no sweet water but that its source springs from under the rock that is in Bayt al-Maqdis.

Qatadah said: It was said: Syria is the outskirts of the abode of emigration; what is lacking from the land is added to Syria, and what is lacking from Syria is added to Palestine. It was said: It is the land of the gathering and the resurrection, the place where people assemble, where Jesus son of Mary will descend, and where Allah will destroy the Dajjal.
